We identify regions of the parameter space that can produce a signal consistent with PTA observations but are in tension with LVK constraints, suggesting that additional mechanisms to suppress the high-frequency spectrum are required for a consistent interpretation of the PTA signal

title: Tidal shells as clocks of galaxy mergers and tests of cosmological models
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures; Proceedings IAU Symposium No. 403, The Hidden Beauty of the Galactic Outskirts
summary: Stellar shells-concentric arc-like tidal features formed in galaxy mergers-provide a valuable record of recent galaxy assembly histories encoding both the merger event and the gravitational potential of the host galaxy. We compare shell systems in observations and cosmological simulations from two complementary perspectives. First, we show that simulations predict a substantial population of very large (>100kpc) shells that are rarely observed, revealing a potentially important discrepancy between simulations and reality. Because the scales of observed and simulated shell systems differ significantly, we focus on a comparison of merger histories. Using a shell-identification method, we estimate merger times for a sample of nearby massive prolate rotators and compare them with merger histories derived from cosmological simulations. We also present ongoing efforts to expand the sample of deeply imaged prolate rotators using observations from the Milankovic telescope, paving the way for future studies based on larger observational samples.

title: Covering Surfaces, Conical-Defect Continuation, and Multi-Entropy at Arbitrary Genus
summary: We derive normalized geometric factors for permutation-twist correlators at arbitrary genus. For three uniformly ramified branch values, hypergeometric uniformization shows that the real part of the continued conical-defect exponent equals the covering-space anomaly factor. Its imaginary part is an Euler-characteristic Weyl phase. We extend the normalization to additional branch values, derive higher replica-index corrections to the geometric multi-entropy, and state the extra condition required for a holographic limit. A reducible conformal/topological example demonstrates why large central charge alone does not fix the complete entanglement result.

title: lenscape: Fast, High-resolution $Δχ^2$ Maps of Microlensing Events
comment: Accepted for publication in AAS journals; 1 figure; code available at https://github.com/hippke/lenscape
summary: Planetary microlensing analyses rely on $Δχ^2$ maps across the binary-lens separation $s$ and mass ratio $q$ to locate degenerate solutions and bound parameter uncertainties. Because every grid point requires a full light-curve optimization with finite-source magnifications, constructing these maps is often the primary computational bottleneck in event modeling. Here I present lenscape, an open-source Python package that accelerates $Δχ^2$ mapping and suppresses local-minimum artifacts through multi-stage neighbor propagation and adaptive contour refinement. Applied to the planetary event MOA-2022-BLG-091, lenscape reproduces the published $50\times50$ map in 14 minutes and generates a $400\times400$ map in under two hours on a desktop computer.

title: Spectra and strong decays of open charm-bottom $c\bar{b}q\bar{q}$ tetraquarks in an unequal-mass Born-Oppenheimer framework
summary: We investigate the mass spectra and strong decay channels of $S$-wave open charm-bottom $c\bar{b}q\bar{q}$ ($q = u,d,s$) tetraquarks within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Extending our previous study of hidden heavy flavor tetraquarks, we account for the unequal-mass heavy quark sources and construct the effective potential based on independently optimized heavy-light orbitals. This makes the computational method more generally applicable. For the quantum numbers $J^P=0^+$, $1^+$, and $2^+$, we have obtained the spectra of the open charm-bottom $c\bar{b}q\bar{q}$ tetraquarks corresponding to color-singlet states constructed by coupling two color octets. The predicted masses exhibit systematic flavor-dependent shifts and characteristic hyperfine splittings. We also estimate partial widths for selected two-body open flavor decay channels using color-spin recoupling and a phenomenological decay prescription. The resulting channel-dependent decay modes, together with comparisons to other theoretical predictions, provide useful benchmarks for future theoretical investigations and experimental searches for open charm-bottom tetraquarks.

title: Apparent horizon mergers in analytic intial data
summary: Five years ago Pook-Kolb, Hennigar and Booth published a series of three papers exploring the evolution of apparent horizons and other marginally outer trapped surfaces during a black hole merger. This was seen to be much more intricate than the well-known "pair-of-pants" merger associated with event horizons. In this paper we show that parameter evolutions of Brill-Lindquist-deSitter initial data mimic many of the features of that evolution. Hence, this analytic intial data is a useful testing ground for ideas about marginally outer trapped surface evolution and spacetime geometry during mergers.

title: Machine Learning Based Classification of Type 1 Active Galactic Nuclei
comment: 14 Figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in A&A
summary:
Aims. We aim to provide a machine learning based method to distinguish type 1 quasars and type 1 Seyfert galaxies based on photometric data, which could be applied to large all-sky surveys. The method can also be used to obtain relatively complete samples of Seyfert galaxy candidates when broad-line AGNs have been selected.
  Results. The results of PCA show that quasars and Seyfert galaxies are partial distinguishable. The supervised classifier based on random forest (RF) achieves good performances for type 1 quasars with a F1 score of 0.967. The performance for classifying Seyfert galaxies is worse, with a F1 score of 0.791. Increasing the classification threshold can help to derive a sample of Seyfert galaxies with high purity. The classifier are then applied to the cross-matched sample with DESI DR1. When compared with the results of spectroscopic classification, quasars also show high precision and recall. For Seyfert galaxies identified by RF classifier, there are plenty of less luminous sources who are classified as quasars by spectroscopic method. If they are regarded as Seyfert galaxies, our classifier also performs well to predict Seyfert galaxies. Both the median SEDs and the fraction of Seyfert galaxies derived by our classifier are similar with those for the training sample, while the fraction of Seyfert galaxies for spectroscopic classification are lower at all redshift. These results indicate that our classifier can recover the features of Seyfert galaxies, at least those similar to the Seyfert galaxies in the training sample.

title: Turbulent gas-rich discs at high redshift: Chaotic orbits and rapid bulge formation at high gas fraction
summary: Using the \nexus\ N-body/hydrodynamic framework, we show that stellar bars that emerge in high-redshift disc galaxies are different in their orbital characteristics compared to their low-redshift counterparts. We identify bar-supporting orbits and, among them, find the fraction of chaotic orbits compared to regular orbits ($f_{\rm chaos}$). This fraction rises above 60\% for models with $f_{\rm gas} > 60 \%$; for $f_{\rm gas} \lesssim 60\%$, we observe chaotic fractions close to zero. The emerging bars seen in the $f_{\rm gas}= 80\%$ and $100\%$ simulations collapse in $\lesssim$1 Gyr to form central bulges supported by rotation, and this collapse follows soon after the chaotic fraction starts to dominate ($f_{\rm chaos} \gtrsim 50\%)$. Moreover, the gravitational potential in those simulations steepens rapidly over that period, and by integrating the chaotic orbits, we find that orbits that deviate from the evolving mean field are more likely to be chaotic. Hence, we argue that the irregularity associated with the rapidly evolving, central potentials drives higher chaotic fractions in these gas-rich bars. As a result, the emergent bars collapse through `violent relaxation' to form oblate rotating bulges. Supporting evidence for this picture comes from the fact that particles of different mass share identical radial profiles, a natural consequence of the rapid relaxation process.

title: Entropically favored scalar hair on AdS black branes
summary: We construct neutral AdS$_5$ black branes with source-free scalar hair that is entropically favored over the symmetric phase. A quadratic scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling destabilizes the thermal state while leaving the ultraviolet operator dimension fixed at $Δ=3$. The fully backreacted solutions require only a quadratic scalar potential. We describe how a neural-network search led to this simple model.

title: UnEZ: A Fully Unsupervised Self-Templating Neural Network for Redshift and Line Strength Estimation
summary: As spectroscopic surveys grow, estimating galaxy properties such as metallicity, star formation rate, and redshift becomes computationally cumbersome. Methods of estimating such properties rely on template spectra or curated redshift catalogs, which fail to represent the diversity of objects seen in large-scale surveys. We present UnEZ, a fully unsupervised, physics-informed machine learning model that can predict spectroscopic redshifts and line strengths with no prior redshift or line strength labels. An encoder predicts emission and absorption line amplitudes/widths, and a fixed deterministic decoder constructs a unique template, estimated redshift, redshift confidence curve, and spectral model. UnEZ was tested on the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Data Release 18 due to its large dataset and thoroughly vetted redshift catalog which serves as an independent benchmark. Despite the lack of templates, line strength labels, or redshift labels, UnEZ's performance competes with modern redshift estimation algorithms. At SNR > 10, UnEZ achieves an outlier fraction of 0.459% and a normalized median absolute deviation (NMAD) of $1.237 \times 10^{-4}$. At SNR > 3, UnEZ achieves an outlier fraction of 3.89% and an NMAD of $1.471 \times 10^{-4}$. Furthermore, we demonstrate how UnEZ's line strength and redshift predictions can be utilized for various purposes such as constructing template spectra required in traditional redshift estimation algorithms. UnEZ illustrates how a fully unsupervised neural network can allow redshift, among other galaxy properties, to emerge naturally from the spectra themselves, providing a template-free, label-free approach that scales to the demands of future surveys.

title: Tracing Electromagnetic Response through Charge Splitting of Directed Flow in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
summary: Experimentally observed charge splitting of directed flow, $Δv_1\equiv v_1(h^+)-v_1(h^-)$, exhibits both a sign reversal at midrapidity and the amplitude change from Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV to Pb+Pb at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$ TeV. We study this behavior within a unified $(3+1)$-dimensional viscous hydrodynamic model that incorporates an electromagnetic source term in the bulk evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and an electromagnetic correction to the Cooper--Frye particlization. The beam-energy dependence of $Δv_1$ can be described by varying the effective electrical conductivity between RHIC and LHC energies, with values consistent with the conductivity scale indicated by lattice-QCD calculations. We find that the sign reversal emerges from the competition between momentum distortions induced by the electric and magnetic field which is controlled by the conductivity during the QGP evolution. The model further predicts the mass-dependent charge splittings for identified pions, kaons, and protons, providing further constraints on their respective relaxation times and the corresponding electromagnetic interaction. These results establish the charge splitting of directed flow as a quantitative probe of the electromagnetic response and the space-time evolution of the QGP.

title: Systematic High Overtone Expansion of Kerr Quasinormal Modes
comment: 37 pages. A Mathematica package is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23691045
summary: We develop a systematic method to compute the high overtone expansion of Kerr quasinormal modes on normal angular branches to arbitrary order. We first obtain the expansion of the angular eigenvalue at large frequencies by a simple polynomial recursion. Using this result in an alternative form of the radial Teukolsky equation, we find that all the WKB corrections are defined on a fixed genus-one spectral curve, and that the quantum periods at the second and higher orders are expressed in terms of only two elliptic periods. This allows us to determine the expansion coefficients order by order. We confirm that the truncated expansions reproduce quasinormal frequencies obtained by solving the angular and radial equations directly, for scalar, electromagnetic and gravitational fields. We also compare the scalar results with the exact WKB analysis of extremal Kerr black holes.

title: Gravitational Dark Matter Production from Spectator Field in $R^2$-Higgs Inflation
summary: We investigate the cosmological gravitational dark matter production of spectator field $χ$ in the multifield $R^2$-Higgs inflation. The spectator field $χ$ couples to gravity only through a non-minimal coupling $ξ_χχ^2R$ and serves as a dark matter (DM) candidate. Working consistently in the Einstein frame, we derive the equation of motion of the background fields and fluctuations at linear order using the doubly covariant formalism. We show the dark matter production and the subsequent comoving relic abundance heavily depend on this effective mass of the field $χ$. Specifically, we find that there exists cancellation regions in the effective mass-squared of $χ$, which ensures the correct relic abundance is achieved. Further, we show that the preheating from Higgs and Goldstone may play critical role in accounting the observed relic density.

title: Unveiling the Shock-Excited Molecular Environment in the Orion Protostar HOPS 370
comment: 4 figures, 12 pages; accepted for publication in the Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy (JoAA)
summary: We present near-infrared K-band ($1.94$--$2.52~μ$m) spectroscopy of the deeply embedded protostellar source HOPS\,370, obtained with the TIFR--ARIES Near Infrared Spectrometer (TANSPEC) on the 3.6-m Devasthal Optical Telescope (DOT). The spectrum is dominated by prominent molecular hydrogen ($\rm H_2$) ro-vibrational emission, with multiple transitions detected from the $1$--$0$ S, $2$--$1$ S, and $1$--$0$ Q branches. Using the intrinsically linked $\rm H_2$ $1$--$0$ Q(3) and $1$--$0$ S(1) transitions, which arise from the same upper energy level, we derive a visual extinction of $A_V = 23.24 \pm 1.25$ mag, corresponding to $A_K = 2.50 \pm 0.13$ mag, consistent with the embedded Class~0/I nature of the source. The diagnostic line ratio $F(2$--$1~{\rm S}(1))/F(1$--$0~{\rm S}(1)) = 0.12 \pm 0.01$ is consistent with thermal excitation and disfavors ultraviolet fluorescence as the dominant excitation mechanism. Assuming optically thin emission and local thermodynamic equilibrium, we derive an $\rm H_2$ excitation diagram that yields an excitation temperature of $2078 \pm 215$ K and a molecular hydrogen column density of $(1.93 \pm 0.93)\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$. We further derive an ortho-to-para ratio of $2.45 \pm 0.21$, indicating substantial shock-driven thermal processing while remaining below the high-temperature equilibrium value of 3. Taken together, these diagnostics indicate that the molecular hydrogen emission in HOPS\,370 originates predominantly in warm, shock-heated gas most likely associated with its protostellar outflow. Our results demonstrate the diagnostic power of combined S- and Q-branch $\rm H_2$ spectroscopy for constraining the physical conditions and excitation history of deeply embedded protostellar systems.

title: Circuit complexity of coupled four-mode squeezed states in two-field inflation
summary: We study the circuit complexity of coupled curvature and entropy perturbations in two-field inflation. We start from the quadratic action and derive the full Hamiltonian. The Hamiltonian includes all diagonal and off-diagonal quadratic terms. We then obtain three coupled equations for the pair amplitudes of the four-mode squeezed state. From these amplitudes, we calculate the two principal squeezing strengths. We use them to determine the Nielsen circuit complexity. For an equal-weight Gaussian circuit, the complexity takes the form $\mathcal{C}_{2,k}=\sqrt{2(r_{1k}^{2}+r_{2k}^{2})}$. It depends on the squeezing strengths but not explicitly on the squeezing angles. Our numerical results show that the complexity grows after horizon crossing in both coupled and uncoupled models. Interfield coupling changes the pair amplitudes and the four-mode squeezed state. However, its effect on the circuit complexity is small for the parameters considered. This result shows that different four-mode pair-amplitude matrices can yield similar values of the chosen equal-weight circuit complexity. The present calculation provides a reference for studying Gaussian circuit complexity in more general two-field inflationary models.

title: SuperCrude EoS: A Simple, Analytical, and Reasonably Accurate Equation of State for Astrophysical Fluid Dynamics
summary: We present SuperCrude, a vastly simplified astrophysical equation of state that captures the most important physics needed for explosive astrophysics, but using compact, physically-motivated analytical approximations rather than precise interpolated data tables. We present a number of code tests demonstrating the performance of SuperCrude in a wide range of parameter space. In large regions of parameter space, SuperCrude is precisely accurate to within the accuracy level of helmeos. For some regions (especially where degeneracy, gas, and radiation are comparable) SuperCrude has errors in its effective adiabatic index on the order of a few percent. The solver's estimate of the temperature is less accurate, on the order of tens of percent. Because the solver is analytic, SuperCrude is designed in such a way to guarantee exact thermodynamic consistency. We incorporate SuperCrude into some hydrodynamic and astrophysical test problems, including the thermonuclear explosion of a white dwarf star. When coupled with a stiff nuclear network, SuperCrude does not achieve the same nucleosynthetic yields as helmeos, motivating future work to improve the temperature accuracy further.

title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
comment: 16 pages including Supplemental Material, 1 figure. Companion code: https://github.com/wuwphy/RGZWorkflow/releases/tag/v1.0.0
summary: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and in the loop sum. Retaining the refined Gribov-Zwanziger masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, retaining contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and by the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms close the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite answer is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not assume colored asymptotic states or establish an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.

title: Physical Effects in the Vicinity of Black Holes
comment: PhD thesis, University of Alberta, Supervisor: Professor Valeri P. Frolov. 204 pages, 16 figures
summary: General relativity, a theory that is already over a century old, is still the best theory that we have to describe the universe at energy scales where only the gravitational force is important. It has stood tall to any observational tests thrown at it since its inception, and it has remarkable predictive power when it is utilized to study and model astrophysical problems. It also continues to surprise us with its ability to generate new problems and insights that render themselves useful in the study of modern physics. This is especially highlighted by the transition of modern observational astronomy away from an electromagnetic radiation epoch, and into a new gravitational wave epoch. This thesis devotes its study to phenomena that can be analyzed within the framework of classical general relativity, but whose results may contain interesting implications for cosmological and black hole observations. (Full abstract can be found in document).

title: Testing Extended Exponential Infrared Teleparallel Gravity with CMB, DESI, and PantheonPlus
summary: We place cosmological constraints on an extended exponential infrared (EExpIR) $f(T)$ teleparallel gravity model using current observational datasets. The extension is characterized by an additional parameter, $b$, which governs the late-time cosmological dynamics. Owing to the existence of two solution branches, phase-space analysis is employed to select the cosmological branch and to establish an appropriate prior range for the new parameter. In this framework, the torsion sector acts as an effective dark-energy component, exhibiting a smooth evolution from a quintessence-like phase to a phantom regime, while recovering the standard cosmological behavior at early times. To constrain the model parameters, we combine early-Universe observations from Planck, ACT, and SPT measurements of the CMB with late-time probes from DESI BAO and PantheonPlus Type Ia supernovae. Using the full dataset, including the SH0ES calibration, we obtain $b=0.573^{+0.016}_{-0.060}$ and $H_0=70.67^{+0.31}_{-0.35}~{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ at 68\% CL. Model comparison based on Bayesian evidence reveals that the EExpIR $f(T)$ and the $Λ$CDM models are statistically indistinguishable when only CMB data are considered, whereas the inclusion of the full cosmological dataset with SH0ES leads to a weak preference in favor of $Λ$CDM.

title: Age-Resolved Vertical Motions in the Milky Way Warp: A Localized Enhancement in Intermediate-Age Populations
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, 1 table, accepted for publication in ApJL. Online Dataset: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23308202
summary: Determining how the Milky Way warp evolves provides constraints on the formation and dynamical evolution of galactic disks. Using Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment Data Release 19 (APOGEE DR19) spectroscopy, we estimate ages for 222,355 red giants. With Gaia astrometry and geometric distances, we analyze 168,824 of these stars in five age bins spanning $0$--$10$ Gyr. The warp-related radial vertical-velocity ($V_Z$) profile of young red giants ($0$--$2$ Gyr) is broadly consistent with those of classical Cepheids and young open clusters. Over $9\leq R<12$ kpc, we find that the mean $V_Z$ values of the intermediate-age red giants ($2$--$4$ and $4$--$6$ Gyr) are $1.48\pm0.46$ and $1.49\pm0.52$ km s$^{-1}$ higher than that of the young population, respectively. By contrast, at $R\simeq12$--$13$ kpc, the $V_Z$ profiles of the $0$--$6$ Gyr red giants are consistent within their uncertainties. The intermediate-age enhancement persists across our robustness tests and may reflect smaller effective kinematic warp onset radii for the intermediate-age populations. The observed velocity differences may arise from the combined effects of earlier perturbations and the present-day warp, or from differences in vertical structure among stellar populations.

title: Tachyon and massless sectors of the bosonic string effective action
summary: Recently, it has been observed that in certain schemes of the bosonic string effective action, the non-derivative tachyon appears only in the tachyon potential, while all other couplings involve covariant derivatives of the tachyon and massless fields. Within these schemes, a minimal basis can be found whose coupling constants are constrained by T-duality upon circle reduction. Using this constraint, one obtains sets of couplings at each order of \(α'\) that are invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the tachyon. In this paper, we observe that consistency of these T-dual sets with S-matrix elements requires an appropriate field redefinition, such that each set becomes invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the metric, dilaton, and tachyon. This separates the couplings into a massless sector and a tachyon sector. We determine the six-derivative couplings in the massless sector, with all coupling constants fixed, and find two T-dual couplings in the tachyon sector with arbitrary coupling constants. We show that the leading-order action and the massless-sector couplings exactly reproduce the expansion of the sphere-level S-matrix element of two tachyons and two massless vertex operators at six-momentum order, and that the coupling constant of the four-tachyon coupling in the tachyon sector is fixed by the expansion of the four-tachyon S-matrix element at six-momentum order.

title: Flow-based neural networks for scalable high resolution imaging of VLBI observations
summary: Bayesian sampling methods in very-long-baseline interferometry enable reliable imaging of astronomical sources with a record high angular resolution. However, even after the transition from classical MCMC methods to flow-based neural networks, they remain computationally expensive as the number of recovered features grows. We used WaveletFlow neural network architecture to increase the number of pixels in the recovered image distribution, addressing the scaling issues of previous models. We applied the algorithm to both model data and archive RadioAstron project observations of M87 and ALMA telescope observations of HL Tau. While yielding comparable fidelity of the individual images, the algorithm provides more statistical information compared to CLEAN, which may be crucial for future research on compact astronomical objects such as active galactic nuclei.

title: Gluon gravitational form factors of the proton from near-threshold charmonium photoproduction
summary: Motivated by near-threshold $J/ψ$ photoproduction measurements, we investigate the gluon contributions to the gravitational form factors (GFFs) of the proton associated with the energy-momentum tensor in quantum chromodynamics. We calculate the gluon GFFs and the corresponding mechanical properties of the proton within a light-front spectator model, in which the proton is described as an active gluon accompanied by a spectator particle. The model parameters are determined from a global fit to the differential cross section for $J/ψ$ photoproduction. The resulting gluon GFFs are in reasonable agreement with recent lattice QCD determinations. We further calculate the total cross section and find reasonable agreement with the available experimental data. Using the extracted gluon GFFs, we investigate the two-dimensional light-front gluon distributions inside the proton, such as the mass, angular momentum, pressure, and shear force distributions. We also study the gluonic contributions to the two-dimensional Galilean energy density, radial and tangential pressures, isotropic pressure, and pressure anisotropy.

title: Gravitational baryogenesis in Gauss-Bonnet braneworld cosmology
summary:
The present study investigates the feasibility of gravitational baryogenesis in a Gauss-Bonnet (GB) modified Randall-Sundrum (RS) type II braneworld cosmology. The modified expansion rate of the Universe in this scenario evolves through three distinct expansion regimes, the GB regime at early times where the expansion rate $H \sim ρ^{1/3}$ falls more slowly than the standard expansion law $H\sim ρ^{1/2}$ of GR, then the RS type era with an enhanced expansion $H \sim ρ$, before finally reducing to the standard expansion law in the low energy limit. Gravitational baryogenesis depends on $\dot{R}$ and requires $\dot{R} <0$. This condition is satisfied for the GB and GR regimes. However, $\dot{R}>0$ for the RS regime and successful baryogenesis requires either that the decoupling temperature occurs during the GB regime or that the Universe makes a direct transition from the GB regime to the GR regime.
  The GB baryon asymmetry $η(T)$ is proportional to $μ(1+w)(1-w)(1+1/β)$, where $μ$ is the energy scale $μ\equiv 1/l$ associated with the bulk curvature scale $l$, $β\equiv 4 αμ^{2}$, where $α$ is the GB coupling, and $w$ is the equation of state parameter $p=w ρ$. Studies of inflation in GB-braneworld cosmology place constraints on the allowed ranges of the parameters $μ$ and $β$. Guided by these, the asymmetry has been calculated for ranges of $(μ, β, w)$ and it is found that the observed values can be obtained for a value of $β$ within the range $(10^{-2} - 10^{-3})$ for $μ=10^{12}$ GeV, and within the range $(10^{-1}- 10^{-2})$ for $μ=10^{13}$ GeV. All values of $η$ for $μ=10^{14}$ are too high. In contrast to GR where $η$ is zero for a radiation dominated Universe ($w=1/3$), it is non-zero in GB braneworld cosmology.

title: Towards constraining cosmology with HI--galaxy cross-correlations from MeerKLASS
summary: We present an inference of cosmological parameters from the cross-correlation power spectrum between the MeerKLASS 2019 L-band HI intensity maps and the overlapping WiggleZ galaxies at $z \simeq 0.43$. The analysis is intended as a proof of concept to verify that the full pipeline, from the foreground cleaning of the maps to the likelihood analysis, can be applied end-to-end to real data and can return results consistent with the concordance cosmology. The model of the observed power spectrum includes observational effects that are relevant to a single-dish experiment. In the most optimistic scenario in which we hold the astrophysical nuisance parameters fixed, we obtain $H_0 = 65.3^{+5.8}_{-10}\text{ km s}^{-1}\text{ Mpc}^{-1}$ and $Ω_{\text{m}} = 0.44^{+0.12}_{-0.30}$ at the 68% confidence level. We find that sampling the HI amplitude with an informative prior retains most of the constraining power and changes these results by less than 1 sigma. Moreover, using synthetic data, we show that neglecting the observational effects in the model biases the inferred parameters by up to 2.5 sigma and also underestimates their uncertainties. Finally, we show that varying the number of foreground modes removed and the range of scales included changes the inferred parameters by less than 0.5 sigma. These results demonstrate the robustness of our pipeline in modelling HI intensity mapping data, and set the foundation for future cosmological inference with intensity mapping using MeerKLASS and SKAO.

title: The Influence of Hubble Expansion on the Future Merger of the Milky Way and Andromeda
comment: 10 pages (+3 pages appendix). Resubmitted to ApJ after referee's report
summary: Most existing idealized simulations of galaxy mergers neglect Hubble expansion, as the local Hubble flow is curved by overdensities and the expansion effect is weak at these scales. However, even in the gravity-dominated Local Group (LG), the expansion itself still persists, and it has been shown important in some LG-related studies. Here we take the future merger of the Milky Way (MW) and Andromeda (M31) as a case study to investigate the differences between simulations with and without Hubble expansion. We perform a suite of idealized N-body simulations of the MW--M31 system under pure Newtonian, $Λ$CDM, and $w_0w_a$CDM scenarios, testing different masses and proper motions of galaxies informed by current observational constraints. At low M31 tangential velocities, especially in cases where the two galaxies merge within a Hubble time, the expansion effect is negligible; while at high velocities (>66.5 km/s), the $Λ$CDM simulations introduce a noticeable delay in the merger time compared to the Newtonian ones and may even alter the final fate of the system, but the caveat here is that the isolated-pair idealization and the assumed expansion history break down. The delay is also present but less pronounced in the $w_0w_a$CDM runs. When M33 and the Large Magellanic Cloud are included, the differences in merger times are reduced. In summary, Hubble expansion can play a noticeable role for galaxy mergers with high tangential velocities, but its actual influence on the MW--M31 merger depends on the precise masses and proper motions to be determined in the future.

title: The Topological String on the Quintic to Genus 83 and the Rank-Two D4-D2-D0 Indices
comment: 46 pages, 4 figures. Code and data: https://github.com/CalabiYau14/paper-topstring-quintic-g83, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23724464
summary: We compute quintic Gopakumar-Vafa invariants for genera 2-83 and degrees up to 44 by integrating the holomorphic anomaly equations. Under rank-one modularity for the required Gieseker invariants and rank-two charge conjugation, a coupled system of boundary and surplus wall-crossing equations fixes the holomorphic ambiguities and 22 of the 36 polar rank-two D4-D2-D0 coefficients, without assuming any rank-two index. A computer-assisted extension of wall crossing supplies additional equations and the boundary datum needed to close the recursion through genus 83. With known low-genus input, the GV data are complete through degree 32 and yield PT and DT tables. Selected higher-genus wall-crossing invariants reach genus 216; 33 entries require additional hypotheses. Retrospectively selected extrapolations give conditional candidates at genera 84 and 85 and, with rank-two mock modularity, for the remaining polar coefficients.

title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
comment: 55 pages, 21 figures, 11 tables. White paper for the Korean Space Telescope (KST). To be Submitted to the Journal of the Korean Astronomical Society (JKAS)
summary: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

title: Inelastic Kinetic Decoupling in WIMP Leptogenesis: A Minimal $Z_4$ Model
summary: We study a minimal $Z_4$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model in which a singlet Dirac fermion $χ$ constitutes dark matter, whose annihilations generate a lepton asymmetry through WIMP leptogenesis. Kinetic equilibrium is maintained mainly by the inelastic conversion $χL\leftrightarrow\barχΨ$. Compared with the near elastic regime, a sizable mass gap suppresses the conversion rate more rapidly as the Universe cools. This naturally drives kinetic decoupling to earlier times, even away from resonance. Starting from the full inelastic collision operator, we derive an effective momentum transfer rate for kinetic decoupling. We then solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the dark matter abundance, its temperature $T_χ$, and the $B-L$ asymmetry. Early kinetic decoupling can significantly modify the relic abundance, although near resonance this modification can be reduced by annihilation-induced heating. The $B-L$ asymmetry can be affected when asymmetry production overlaps with a substantial departure from kinetic equilibrium. In our scan, the largest deviations occur mainly for $x_{\rm lep}\gtrsim x_{\rm cd}$. After imposing our constraints, asymmetry production typically ends before chemical decoupling, leaving the final asymmetry essentially unchanged. For indirect detection, we generate the photon spectrum with Pythia and evaluate the Fermi-LAT dwarf spheroidal likelihood.

title: Axion-angle dependence of the rotational and tidal properties of PNJL quark stars
summary: We investigate how a fixed, spatially uniform axion angle modifies the rotational and static tidal properties of self-bound quark stars in general relativity, using an axion-extended Polyakov-loop Nambu--Jona-Lasinio equation of state. We vary $θ$ from $0$ to $π$ while holding the remaining model parameters fixed, and compute the leading-order moment of inertia and the second-order spin-induced quadrupole moment and mass shift. The calculation includes finite-surface-density contributions to the rotational mass shift and static tidal response. Across this range, the static maximum mass increases from $1.68$ to $1.95\,M_\odot$, remaining below the lower edge of the quoted $1σ$ timing interval for PSR~J0740+6620. At $M=1.338\,M_\odot$, the moment of inertia increases by $13\%$ and the dimensionless tidal deformability rises from $342$ to $547$. Over the common mass range examined, the differences in the moment of inertia between adjacent sampled angles exceed the tested interpolation and table-resolution sensitivities. Despite these changes, joint fits to the five sequences describe the $\bar I$--$C$ and I-Love-Q relations with maximum departures of $2.7\%$ and $0.4\%$, respectively, over the fitted domains. The predicted binary tidal-deformability curves lie within the estimated 90\% credible region of the adopted GW170817 posterior over the mass-ratio ranges examined. Within this EOS family, stellar properties vary appreciably with $θ$, while the normalized quantities admit accurate joint fits across the five sequences.

title: Probing the local primordial non-Gaussianity with clustering of FRB dispersion measure and galaxies
summary: We forecast the sensitivity of a joint fast radio burst (FRB) and galaxy survey to local primordial non-Gaussianity using the full $3\times2$-point statistic: the angular dispersion-measure (DM) auto-spectrum, the DM-galaxy cross-spectrum, and the galaxy auto-spectrum. Local primordial non-Gaussianity imprints a scale-dependent bias on both the free-electron field probed by FRB dispersion measures and the galaxy field. Hence, all three spectra carry information on the local non-Gaussianity amplitude $f_{\rm NL}$. Adopting a DESI-like luminous-red-galaxy sample and an FRB population over 35% of the sky, we forecast $σ(f_{\rm NL}) \simeq 5$ for both $N_{\rm FRB} = 10^4$ and $10^5$ at fixed Planck 2018 cosmology, marginalised over three astrophysical bias parameters $(b_e^0, z_{\rm fb}, b_g^{\rm amp})$. The $f_{\rm NL}$ constraint is robust to marginalising over the six $Λ$CDM parameters $(ω_b, ω_{\rm cdm}, h, A_s, n_s, τ)$ with Planck priors. At these sample sizes, the galaxy auto-spectrum sets the constraint, while the DM sector's contribution grows with the burst count and becomes decisive for the larger samples anticipated in the SKA era, reaching $σ(f_{\rm NL}) \simeq 2$ at $10^7$ bursts.

title: GRAVITY-RESOLVE: A comprehensive image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations with GRAVITY
comment: Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A) on October 24, 2026
summary: We aim to improve and extend the imaging capabilities of the GRAVITY beam combiner instrument of ESOs VLTI with respect to reconstruction software in the Galactic Center. We revise and develop the image reconstruction code GRAVITY-RESOLVE $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, which has been specifically developed to reconstruct stars in the Galactic Center with GRAVITY. The main objectives are to increase the limiting magnitude in GRAVITY images, reduce its computational runtime, and allow for a joint reconstruction of multiple, spatially separate datasets/pointings on sky. We apply $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ to recent GRAVITY data, featuring the implemented GRAVITY-faint mode as part of GRAVITY+, the upgrade of GRAVITY. We reconstruct visibility phases and amplitudes and present the first GRAVITY image reconstructed with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ from these quantities. We demonstrate NIR mosaicking with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ by jointly reconstructing nine separately acquired datasets of 2025 into a single image on a scale of $\simeq 3390\ \text{AU}\times 3390\ \text{AU}$, corresponding to $409.6\ \text{mas}\times 409.6\ \text{mas}$. With dedicated injection tests of point sources into GRAVITY data, we estimate the limiting magnitude to be $m_{\text{K}}\ \simeq\ 20.0$ within a radius of $25\ \text{mas}$ around the field center when reconstructing from closure phases and visibility amplitudes. We report on the discovery of two new faint stars in the Galactic Center: S303 and S304. Finally, we find a decrease in computational runtime by a factor of at least $\sim10$. With $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, we demonstrate GRAVITYs capabilities for NIR imaging. We show that $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ is a fast, precise, and deep image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations, enabling the discovery of even more faint stars.

title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlevé Equation
summary: For the first Painlevé equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_π\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-π}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8π/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2π/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlevé transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.

title: Tabular Foundation Models Dramatically Outperform Bespoke Photometric Redshift Estimators
comment: Accepted for 9th Workshop on Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS 2026)
summary: Estimating galaxy redshifts (a proxy for distance) from imaging data alone, also known as photometric redshifts (photo-$z$'s), is essential for studies of extragalactic astrophysics and cosmology. However, data-driven estimators rely on spectroscopic training datasets, which are scarce and systematically biased toward bright and easily observed galaxies. In this work, we show that tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose synthetic pretraining amounts to a learned prior over regression problems, can outperform bespoke estimators using only in-context learning. Evaluating on a widely used benchmark dataset, we find that TFMs predicting full probability distributions in a single forward pass systematically outperform bespoke estimators across both representative and biased training data regimes, matching or exceeding baselines trained on over $40{,}000$ galaxies with just $1{,}000$ training context examples. We also show that the TFM advantage is largest when little to no calibration data are available, and that it persists even when the bespoke baselines are supplemented with up to $10{,}000$ representative calibration spectra. This shows that TFMs offer a sample-efficient framework for upcoming imaging-only astronomical surveys, where observational selection bias can be mitigated simply by including a small representative calibration sample in context.

title: Nonlinear response and retarded three-point correlators of charge transport
comment: 14 pages. Any questions and comments welcome
summary: We study nonlinear response of charge transport in relativistic kinetic theory within the relaxation time approximation. For a classical gas of massless charged particles coupled to an external $U(1)$ gauge field, we organize the Boltzmann equation perturbatively in the source and derive a recursive solution for the distribution function to arbitrary response order. At second order we analytically obtain fully retarded three-point correlators at generic frequencies and momenta, verify the Ward identities implied by charge conservation. We also discuss the general properties of these correlators, including their analytic structure, consistency limits, and relation to Schwinger--Keldysh effective theories of diffusive fluctuations.

title: Hamiltonian Analysis of the Newer General Relativity
summary: We present a systematic Hamiltonian analysis of the five-parameter class of theories known as Newer General Relativity. Quadratic nonmetricity theories of this type can be divided into nine types according to the structure of their primary constraints. After reviewing the framework of symmetric teleparallel gravity, we derive the ADM formulation of Newer General Relativity, discuss the existing classification and perform the Hamiltonian formulation of the theory. For each type, we compute the conjugate momenta, identify the primary constraints, and construct both the canonical and primary Hamiltonians. We then determine the constraint structure and analyze the resulting physical degrees of freedom in each type.

title: Running cosmological constant in light of recent CMB-BAO data
summary: We revisit single-field slow-roll inflation driven by a running cosmological constant, i.e. a cosmological constant receiving a logarithmic radiative correction, in light of the latest CMB-BAO data. The relative radiative correction $δ$ is treated as a free parameter of the model and allowed to be positive or negative. For positive $δ$, the predictions interpolate between a logarithmic regime and a linear inflation one. Compatibility with CMB-only data is confined to a narrow stripe near the $2σ$ border where $δ$ is relatively large. On the other hand, the predictions fit easily within the constraints including BAO data in a wide range of parameters. For negative $δ$, the slow-roll approximation breaks down at small field values and the predictions are excluded by data. However, once the effective mass contribution inside the logarithmic correction is taken into account, the negative $δ$ potential develops a local maximum and behaves like a hilltop model, achieving compatibility with CMB-only data, while agreement with CMB-BAO data is possible only at $2σ$.

title: The nature of the Norma arm as a bar-driven star-forming shock front
summary: The Milky Way is commonly depicted as having four major spiral arms, including the Norma-Outer arm, and a central stellar bar whose properties remain debated. Masers associated with young high-mass stars have been used to trace a segment of the "Norma arm" extending from one end of the Galaxy's central stellar bar. Recent work suggests that these masers may reside along a spiral arm or occupy the dominant x1 stellar orbits that give the bar its shape. We now use a new generation of N-body, hydrodynamic simulations to argue that these million-year old masers instead trace the Galactic bar's Quadrant I shock front or, equivalently, its dust lane. This implies that the bar dust-lane is star-forming, shedding new light on our understanding of star formation processes in the Milky Way. By associating the masers with the simulated shock front, we determine the bar's parameters to be: a ~ 4.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, b ~ 2.3 +/- 0.2 kpc, phi = 20 (+5/-2) deg, Omega_p <~ 40 km s^-1 kpc^-1, representing the bar's semi-major and semi-minor half-lengths, inclination angle and pattern speed, respectively. This raises questions about the Milky Way's spiral structure and suggests that the Galactic bar is long, slow and star-forming.

title: The Non-Relativistic Limit of Five-Dimensional Boson Stars and Scale Invariance Violation
summary: We investigate the non-relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in (4+1)-dimensional general relativity (GR). In this limit, the resulting Newtonian theory exhibits an exact scale invariance, leading to a critical boson star configuration with a fixed global U(1) charge and vanishing binding energy. We identify the origin of these properties in the restored scale symmetry and analyze how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry. By comparing the full (4+1)-dimensional Einstein-Klein-Gordon system with the Wick-Cutkosky model, we quantify the effects of these corrections on the energy-charge relation and the kinematic stability of the configurations. Our results demonstrate how weak violation of scale invariance lifts the degeneracy of the non-relativistic solutions and determines the behavior of boson stars away from the critical limit.

title: Towards an Astronomical Use of New-Generation Geodetic Observations
comment: PhD thesis, Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM). Supervisors: Iván Martí-Vidal and Rafael Bachiller García. Defended on 19 October 2026. 230 pages
summary:
This thesis explores the astronomical use of observations from the VLBI Global Observing System (VGOS), a next-generation geodetic network designed to improve the precision of terrestrial and celestial reference frames and Earth orientation parameters. Although primarily conceived for geodesy, its wide frequency coverage and regular monitoring of compact active galactic nuclei (AGN) provide valuable opportunities for astrophysics.
  We develop a calibration pipeline that transforms VGOS correlator outputs into full-polarization, calibrated visibilities suitable for astronomical imaging. The procedure combines linear-to-circular polarization conversion, instrumental phase and amplitude calibration, and a new wideband global fringe-fitting algorithm that accounts for dispersive ionospheric effects. Regularized maximum likelihood imaging is then used to reconstruct multi-frequency intensity and polarimetric images.
  The pipeline is applied to the blazar 1803+784 and five additional AGN: 3C418, 0059+581, 0613+570, 1849+670, and 2229+695. We measure frequency-dependent core shifts, spectral indices, and Faraday rotation properties. For 1803+784, the fitted core-shift index is $k_r = 0.73^{+0.12}_{-0.19}$, suggesting departures from a simple conical jet in energy equipartition.
  Finally, we apply the reconstructed source models to correct structure-dependent effects in geodetic VLBI observables. The correction reduces closure-delay scatter and post-fit residuals for strongly structured sources, particularly 3C418, while its effectiveness depends on source variability and the temporal proximity of the imaging observations.
  These results demonstrate the dual scientific value of VGOS as a powerful multi-frequency astronomical VLBI instrument and as a means of improving geodetic measurements.

title: Two-loop BRST-restoring finite counter-terms for chiral non-abelian gauge theories
summary: We study the renormalization of anomaly-free chiral $SU(N)$ gauge theories without scalar fields through two-loop order. We adopt the Breitenlohner--Maison--'t Hooft--Veltman (BMHV) scheme for the treatment of $γ_5$ in dimensional regularization. This prescription induces spurious breaking of BRST symmetry, requiring finite symmetry-restoring counter-terms in addition to the subtraction of ultraviolet divergences. We derive these counter-terms for a general, possibly reducible fermion representation, thus restoring the BRST symmetry, through two loops.

title: Quasinormal Modes of a Rotating Hořava Black Hole: Two Perturbative Approaches to Nonseparability
summary: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) provide a powerful probe of strong-field gravity. We study fundamental scalar quasinormal modes of an asymptotically flat rotating black hole in the low-energy sector of Hořava gravity, whose exact scalar equation is nonseparable due to rotation-induced Lorentz violation. We develop two complementary approximations that both preserve the exact Kerr sector: Method I applies a slow-rotation approximation only to the nonseparable Lorentz-violating part, whereas Method II employs a small-$η$ biorthogonal spheroidal projection, with $η$ the Lorentz-violating parameter. Using residual-controlled continuation and symmetric finite differences, validated by a Kerr continued-fraction benchmark and an independent radial spectral method, we compute the linear frequency response. Axisymmetric modes provide an exact Kerr null test. For the corotating modes studied, the real-frequency response is positive and increases with spin. At $a/M=0.9$, the two methods reveal a roughly $2\%$ angular correction to the real response, while the imaginary response is nonmonotonic and highly sensitive to angular projection due to internal cancellation. These results highlight the distinct rotational signatures of Lorentz violation in black-hole ringdown.

title: Cosmic birefringence tomography with radio galaxies I: Testing birefringence solutions to the CMB-BAO tension
summary: We present an independent test of cosmic birefringence induced by axionlike particles (ALPs) at low redshift using radio galaxies. We focus on models that can alleviate the mild tension between recent baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements and observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). This tension can be explained by a large cosmic birefringence rotation angle generated during the reionization epoch. Such a large rotation can arise if the recent isotropic cosmic birefringence measurements are subject to an $nπ$ phase ambiguity, with $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, or if cold dark matter injects energy into ALPs. We constrain these two scenarios by fitting the cosmic birefringence angles estimated from the jet morphologies and polarization angles of radio galaxies obtained by Battye, Jackson & Browne (2026). For the $nπ$ model, the radio-galaxy data exclude $|n|\geq 1$ at more than $2σ$ for $\log_{10}(m_φ/{\rm eV})\lesssim -30.7$. For the energy injection model, the data are consistent with no energy injection, but with a slight relative preference for a nonzero energy injection compared to the no-injection case. Since our samples are limited to $\sim 3000$ and there could still be several astrophysical uncertainties and statistical fluctuations, further exploration of tomographic cosmic birefringence using a large number of low-redshift radio galaxies is important for independent tests of cosmic birefringence.

title: Kinematic methods of spiral nature identification: limitations and applicability
summary: The nature of spiral arms in galaxies remains debated, with several competing formation scenarios, including density waves, kinematic spirals, dynamic spirals, and recurrent modes, that are difficult to distinguish observationally. We tested two kinematic methods - the phase reversal method and the velocity harmonic dominance method - using toy models and mock data from TNG50 simulations. For bar resonances, the phase reversal method is strongly orientation-dependent and yields reliable corotation estimates only when the bar is aligned with the disc minor axis. For spiral arms, the phase reversal method does not always yield reliable results and should be used in tondem with another kinematic method. The velocity harmonic dominance method is more robust: it distinguishes between density wave, kinematic, and dynamic spiral patterns, although it still shows some sensitivity to orientation. Uncertainties in the rotation curve do not strongly affect its results. We also apply both methods to the observed grand-design spiral galaxy NGC3938 as an illustrative example; the results suggest the presence of multiple spiral modes, consistent with the recurrent modes scenario and this interpretation relies on different indirect evidence. Based on our findings, we propose a strategy for classifying spiral structure in observed galaxies that combines multiple independent tests. Applying this analysis to an extended sample will allow us to validate its predictive power and to investigate the diversity of spiral formation scenarios.

title: Conformal Spectrum of (Super) Chiral Ising and XY Models
summary: We determine the spectrum of scaling dimensions of composite operators in the critical Gross-Neveu-Yukawa and Nambu-Jona-Lasinio-Yukawa models through a next-to-leading order semiclassical computation. Their infrared fixed points belong to the chiral Ising and chiral XY universality classes, respectively. At next-to-leading order, we resolve the Lorentz structure of the operator spectrum. For the parameter values at which supersymmetry is expected to emerge in the infrared, we obtain a closed-form expression encoding the full spectrum within the semiclassical methodology. The resulting organization of operators into superconformal multiplets provides further evidence for emergent superconformal dynamics.

title: Search for Cosmic Rays in GRANDProto300
comment: Presented at the 60th Rencontres de Moriond on Very High Energy Phenomena in the Universe (Moriond VHEPU 2026). 4 pages, 1 figure
summary: GRANDProto300 is a prototype array of the GRAND experiment, designed to validate the technique of autonomous radio-detection of astroparticles by detecting cosmic rays with energies between 10$^{17} - 10^{18.5}$ eV. This observation will further enable the study of the Galactic-to-extragalactic source transition region. Between November 2024 and June 2025, 46 antennas were operational, and since July 2025, 63 antennas have been collecting data stably. We present here our cosmic-ray search pipeline, that involves several filtering steps: (1) exclusion of clustered (in time and space) noise events, (2) polarization cut, (3) zenith arrival cut, and (4) delay in expected trigger cut. The efficiency is evaluated on the latest batch of data from July 2025 to October 2025. Additionally, we present an identification layer that is being developed: a CNN-based algorithm to discriminate between noise and cosmic-ray signals, using signal traces. We present the accuracy of our model, trained both on simulations and on real cosmic-ray signal datasets.

title: Probing micron-range fifth forces with cold atoms in optical tweezer arrays
summary: We propose a new method to search for fifth forces at micron scales, by resonantly exciting the motional state of ground-state-cooled atoms in optical tweezer arrays. We develop a homodyne readout protocol based on sideband thermometry, which can approach the Standard Quantum Limit, and expand the discovery reach for fifth forces by up to four orders of magnitude compared to existing constraints. We show that this level of sensitivity can also probe well-motivated models of extra dimensions beyond the current tabletop state of the art, by leveraging the parametric enhancement of higher-dimensional gravity.

title: Exact Rotating Wormholes in Five Dimensions and Their Exceptional-Point Instability
summary: We give an independent closed-form construction of rotating five-dimensional Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes with equal angular momenta and analyze the radial instability of the reflection-symmetric family. The nontrivial coupled metric equations reduce exactly to an open $A_2$ Toda system. The general two-ended solution is expressed in terms of elementary Toda tau functions; the symmetric subclass reduces to a particularly simple one-parameter family interpolating between the static wormhole and the extremal equal-spin Myers--Perry geometry. On this exact background we revisit the cohomogeneity-one perturbation problem. Besides the ordinary unstable mode of the static wormhole, rotation renders the descendant of its non-normalizable zero mode normalizable. The two purely imaginary unstable frequencies coalesce at $|J|/A=0.100628$, where their eigenvectors coalesce as well, identifying a second-order exceptional point. Beyond it the pair continues as $ω_\pm=\pmω_R+\mathrm iω_I$ with $ω_I>0$: the apparent loss of the radial instability found in the original real-eigenvalue treatment is therefore not stabilization, but a transition to an oscillatory instability. We follow this branch deep into the rapidly rotating regime, where its growth rate becomes strongly suppressed.

title: Cosmological axion-photon interactions with a nonminimal dark gauge sector
summary: We study the cosmological evolution of radiation and dark radiation with nonminimal axion-photon-dark photon couplings. The Chern-Simons-type axion-gauge field interactions between the dark and visible sectors can induce energy conversion between photons and dark photons as well as polarization rotation during the propagation of radiation, leading to CMB spectral distortions and cosmic birefringence. Using the observed CMB monopole spectrum, we constrain the photon-dark photon energy conversion fraction, which is determined by the coupling constants and the evolution of the axion field. We further show that the parity-odd mixing interaction $φF\tilde{B}$ can partially relax the constraints on the standard axion-photon coupling, $φF\tilde{F}$, derived from the current observational limits of the cosmic birefringence angle.

title: Chemodynamical Study and Evidence for Hot Compact Companions to Blue Straggler Stars in Berkeley 31
comment: 27 pages, including 14 figures and 4 tables, accepted for publication in the The Astrophysical Journal (ApJ)
summary: We present a detailed study of the open cluster Berkeley 31 using Gaia DR3 astrometry, Gaia-ESO Survey DR5.1 spectroscopy, and multi-wavelength photometry. We identify 329 probable cluster members from their proper motions and trigonometric parallaxes and use them to examine the cluster's fundamental parameters, stellar populations, and Galactic orbit. The cluster is located at a distance of $6024 \pm 181$ pc, with a color excess of $E(B-V)=0.148 \pm 0.047$ mag, and has a mean metallicity of [Fe/H] $=-0.36 \pm 0.04$ dex and $\langle [α/{\rm Fe}] \rangle=0.21 \pm 0.04$ dex. Isochrone fitting gives an age of $3.7 \pm 0.2$ Gyr, consistent with the independent chemical-clock estimate of $3.72 \pm 1.42$ Gyr. The systemic radial velocity is $57.89 \pm 0.08$ km s$^{-1}$. We find that about 38% of the MS stars are unresolved binary candidates with $q \gtrsim 0.5$. We identify 62 BSSs and 2 YSS candidates, including 48 BSSs and both YSSs not previously reported in the literature. We constructed multi-wavelength SEDs for these stars, including Swift/UVOT data for 28 BSSs. Two BSSs show clear ultraviolet excesses and are consistent with compact hot companions, one with a hot WD and the other with a pre-ELM WD. The present orbital parameters give a guiding radius of $12.29 \pm 0.29$ kpc and an eccentricity of $0.11 \pm 0.01$. Comparison with the estimated chemical birth radius indicates a moderate outward shift of the guiding center, with the present orbital position also contributing to the radial displacement. These results consistently describe Berkeley 31 as an intermediate-age, metal-poor outer-disk cluster and place its stellar populations in the context of its Galactic dynamical history.

title: Bootstrapping Wilson lines in Critical Bosonic QED$_3$ Part 1: Large-$N$ endpoint correlators and CFT data
summary: We study the conformal Wilson line with general charge $q$ in critical bosonic QED$_3$ with $N$ complex scalar flavors by combining diagrammatic four-point calculations with endpoint crossing. We formulate the endpoint crossing equations with the full $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ flavor structure, keeping positivity manifest. For arbitrary positive integer charge $q$ held fixed at large $N$, we obtain closed-form expressions for four-endpoint correlators and mixed correlators involving two bulk Hubbard--Stratonovich fields through first subleading order in $1/N$. These results determine the endpoint dimension, the defect $g$-function, and the dimensions and endpoint OPE coefficients of the lowest non-singlet Wilson-line primaries. Moreover, combining the diagrammatic correlator with endpoint crossing, somewhat surprisingly, we find agreement between the bulk and Wilson-line spectra in every non-singlet flavor channel through order $1/N$. At degenerate levels, this agreement concerns the OPE-weighted averages of anomalous dimensions probed by the endpoint correlator. For unit charge, we independently reproduce these averages from the known bulk higher-spin spectrum.

authors: Nils Heyer for the RNO-G Collaboration
title: The Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland (RNO-G) - System Design and Instrumentation
comment: Presented at the Topical Workshop on Electronics for Particle Physics - TWEPP2026
summary: The Radio Neutrino Observatory in Greenland (RNO-G) is designed to measure cosmic neutrinos in the EeV range through an array of radio antennas detecting nanosecond-long radio flashes. In this contribution, the RNO-G electronic system is outlined, illustrating how signals are measured from the antennas to the recorded pulses. We present new instrumentation developments, focusing on electric melters to install LPDA antennas into the Greenlandic ice sheet. The new system will simplify deployment and reduce positioning uncertainty to $\pm$2cm (x/y) and $\pm$1°(rotational). We report on field tests from the RNO-G site at Summit Station.

title: Collinear Factorization and Evolution
comment: 21 pages, 7 figures. Contribution to the Elsevier Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics
summary: The method of collinear factorization for high-energy inclusive cross sections has found wide use in the analysis of hadronic collisions. We introduce the form of factorized cross sections, and discuss the roles and definitions of parton distributions, hadronic fragmentation functions, and their evolution, starting with parton model concepts. The Drell-Yan process is used to illustrate the calculation of QCD corrections at next-to-leading order. The special role of deep-inelastic scattering structure functions and their relation to hadronic structure are also briefly discussed. We provide an introduction to all-order arguments for factorization and infrared safety, and close with a brief review of related factorization formalisms.

title: Resonance correction to time-dependent finite-size effects in Effective Field Theory of binary black hole inspiral
summary: General Relativity predicts that black holes lack an internal structure and that their tidal Love numbers vanish. However, if astrophysical black holes were instead ultra-compact objects (UCOs) with internal structure, their tidal Love numbers would no longer vanish. Then, during a binary inspiral, their tidal deformation could transfer orbital energy to the UCO, increasing the orbital period and leaving an observable imprint on the phase of the emitted gravitational waves. As we discussed previously, the effect is enhanced if one binary companion is resonantly excited. Here we use the point-particle effective field theory framework to calculate this enhancement. We consider circular orbits and focus on excitations of the internal electric quadrupole, modelling the UCO spectrum as a harmonic oscillator spectrum. However, our methods could be straightforwardly extended to more complicated situations. Integrating out the internal quadrupole induces a series of time-dependent finite-size operators with specific numerical coefficients, which we calculate. We find that the static electric quadrupole Love number $k_2$ is negative, and that all finite-size terms are proportional to $k_2$. We further show that resonant excitation induces a leading 2.5 Post-Newtonian term, compared with the 5 Post-Newtonian term in the time-independent case. Our results confirm the expectation that resonant excitation during a binary inspiral offers one of the best ways to detect whether astrophysical black holes can undergo tidal deformation and, if they do, learn about their internal excitation spectrum.

title: A deep learning approach to member identification and mass estimation in galaxy clusters
comment: 16 pages, 13 figures, 5 tables. Accepted by Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Accurate dynamical mass estimates of galaxy clusters are essential for studies of cluster formation and evolution and for cosmological applications. However, interloper galaxies, which are not gravitationally bound to the cluster but are incorrectly identified as members, can bias dynamical mass measurements and increase uncertainties. We developed a probabilistic deep-learning framework for cluster member identification and dynamical mass estimation and tested sensitivity to cluster miscentring and radially dependent incompleteness in controlled mock experiments. We used mock galaxy cluster catalogues to train a two-stage model. A long short-term memory (LSTM) network assigns membership probabilities to galaxies arranged by projected phase-space proximity. These probabilities construct membership-weighted projected phase-space density maps, from which a Bayesian neural network (BNN) infers cluster masses and predictive uncertainties. The LSTM membership probabilities are well calibrated and form an isoprobability envelope in projected phase space, with the $\langle p_{\rm mem}\rangle = 0.5$ contour broadly tracing the empirical member--interloper transition. A threshold of $p_{\rm th} = 0.5$ balances member completeness and purity, with high completeness within $R_{\rm proj} < r_{200}$. Membership weighting lowers the residual scatter of the fiducial BNN mass estimator, $\mathrm{BNN}^{\mathrm{Mem}}_{\mathrm{2D}}$, to $σ_ε= 0.120$, a 19.5% reduction relative to the unweighted baseline, although predictive uncertainties are not uniformly calibrated across BNN models. Using the brightest cluster galaxy rather than the gravitational centre lowers the median inferred mass by up to 47.6%, with larger reductions at larger centring offsets. By contrast, removing 40% of eligible non-central galaxies within $r_{200}$ lowers it by 6.1% relative to complete catalogues.

title: On The Scaling Relations Between Black Holes And The Galaxy/Bulge Mass And Their Connections With The Black Hole Occupation Fraction
comment: 17 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to ApJ, comments welcome!
summary: We investigate the black hole (BH)--host galaxy scaling relations predicted by the semianalytic model \texttt{FEGA25}, focusing on their dependence on BH mass threshold, galaxy morphology, and redshift, and on their connection with the BH occupation fraction (BHOF). Using the YS200 cosmological simulation as our reference volume, we study the $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\star}$ and $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\rm bulge}$ relations for different BH mass selections and compare their redshift evolution with the hydrodynamical zoom-in simulation \texttt{NewCluster}. We find that BH mass cuts primarily affect the low-mass regime, while the selected relations progressively converge toward the intrinsic no-cut relations at higher host masses. The $M_{\rm BH}$--$M_{\star}$ relation also depends systematically on galaxy morphology, with increasingly bulge-dominated systems preferentially occupying higher stellar masses. Over $z=0$--$3$, FEGA25 shows no clear systematic evolution of either scaling relation, consistent with a broadly preserved statistical connection between BH and host-galaxy growth. NewCluster shows no clear monotonic evolution either, although it exhibits larger scatter, particularly toward high host masses. We further show that BHOF and BH--host scaling relations encode complementary information. A low BHOF generally corresponds to a stronger selection-induced offset, but the mapping is not unique: substantially different occupation fractions can yield similar median scaling relations, and at fixed BHOF the bias depends on the host property and underlying BH mass distribution. At $z=0$, \texttt{FEGA25} is consistent with available observational constraints for both stellar- and bulge-mass relations, while predicting increased scatter and bending toward lower host masses.

authors: with an appendix by Xingyang Yu
title: Topological interfaces between universes and generalized families of 2d QFTs
summary: Two-dimensional quantum field theories with topological point operators decompose into universes. Just as fusion categories have played an important role in understanding non-invertible symmetries, multi-fusion categories play an analogous role for the symmetries of such decomposing theories. We describe a finite symmetry as a multi-fusion category together with its action functor, which keeps track of trivially acting symmetries and of the topological interfaces between universes. Relative to a chosen symmetry, we classify pairs of universes by the topological interfaces it contains, which reflect the structure of the multi-fusion category: universes in different indecomposable summands are joined by no interface (Type~III), while within a summand they are related by invertible (Type~I) or only non-invertible (Type~II) interfaces. For orbifolds with a trivially acting abelian normal subgroup, we derive the full inherited symmetry, which characterizes the operators between universes found case by case by Robbins, Sharpe and Vandermeulen and yields pairs of Types~I and~II but never of Type~III. We construct Type~III pairs instead from extensions of $2$-group type and from renormalization group flows out of a common ultraviolet theory. Finally, we propose a correspondence with the generalized families of quantum field theories of Brennan and Intriligator, in which equivariant families correspond to Type~I pairs and categorical ones to Type~II pairs whose gauging preserves the symmetry, family anomalies appear as universes carrying different symmetry-protected topological phases, and Type~III pairs can realize families over a discrete parameter. An appendix by Xingyang Yu works out the higher-charge Schwinger model as a Lagrangian example.

title: Robust statistical significance for Gravitational Wave inference
summary: The field of gravitational-wave data analysis heavily relies on Bayes factors to make statements about astrophysical effects in events detected by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration. This is true on an event level, for example when discussing the potential detection of precession or eccentricity, as well as on a population level. For the latter, perhaps the main limiting factor is the reliance on the output from event-level nested sampling analyses, which is known to introduce growing uncertainties and biases as the number of detections increases. In both cases, while Bayes factors are useful when comparing different models, because the underlying distribution of Bayes factors in noise is unknown, it is often not possible to use them to make quantifiable statistical statements. Their statistical meaning is also questionable in the at least $20\%$ of gravitational-wave events that contain transient noise artifacts. This paper shows that it is possible to use evidence networks, which can infer Bayes factors after learning the distinguishability between datasets, to solve all of the aforementioned problems. By being able to calculate up to $10^5$ Bayes factors per second, we can construct background distributions of Bayes factors under different signal assumptions to estimate significance. We show that the high precision achieved allows us to scale the results from up to $10^4$ events with no discernable bias on population-level quantities, while laying the foundations for a likelihood-free method that does not rely on the assumption of Gaussian and stationary noise.

title: Precision Studies of Boosted Polarized Vector Bosons with Energy Correlators
summary: Boosted, hadronically decaying $W$ and $Z$ bosons are among the most abundant heavy objects at colliders, and their vector nature makes their substructure qualitatively richer than that of a scalar. We initiate precision studies of the hadronic decays of boosted polarized vector bosons with energy correlators. In the narrow-width limit, the laboratory-frame two-point energy correlator is a sum of longitudinal and transverse decay spectra, each weighted by its polarized production rate and obtained by a closed-form boost kernel acting on rest-frame correlators. Combining polarized production density matrices, computed at NNLO in QCD for $pp\to V+X$ and at leading order for $e^+e^-\to W^+W^-$, with decay correlators that combine NNLO fixed order with NNLL collinear and N$^4$LL back-to-back resummation, we find for high-$p_T$ $W/Z$ production that polarization shifts the spectrum by $\mathcal{O}(10\%)$ relative to a naive unpolarized treatment. Even without any reconstruction, hadronic $W/Z$ decays stand out over the realistic QCD background of untagged jet samples as a localized angular bump. Our results open the door to using energy correlators for polarimetry of electroweak bosons through their hadronic decays, for standard-candle measurements of electroweak bosons inside jets, and in sharper searches for new resonances.

title: Gravitational field of spinors with torsion and matter$-$antimatter asymmetry
summary: The conservation law for the orbital plus spin angular momentum of a free Dirac particle in curved spacetime requires that the affine connection has the antisymmetric part: the torsion tensor, which extends general relativity to the Einstein$-$Cartan theory of gravity.
