In spacetime with torsion, the Dirac equation becomes a nonlinear, cubic equation in the spinor wave function. Under charge conjugation, the nonlinear term changes sign relative to the mass term. A Dirac spinor and its charge conjugate therefore satisfy different field equations. We use the spinor connection formalism to derive the Dirac equation for a spherical spinor in its centrally symmetric gravitational field with torsion. We determine the energy$-$momentum tensor for this spinor and show that the energy contribution from torsion is negative for matter particles and positive for antimatter particles. Consequently, the ground state of a fermion has a lower energy than the ground state of the corresponding antifermion. We also derive the Einstein$-$Cartan$-$Dirac equations for this spinor; they indicate the existence of particle-like soliton solutions exhibiting matter$-$antimatter energy asymmetry.

title: Low-variance renoising for weak gravitational lensing shear estimation
summary: The "renoising" noise-bias correction used by Metacalibration and AnaCal adds to every galaxy image an independent noise field with the statistics of the original noise rotated by 90 degrees. The rotated field cancels, to first order in shear, the anisotropy that the shear-response operation induces in the original noise, at the cost of doubling the noise variance. We derive the general condition that an added noise field must satisfy for this cancellation: the distribution of the total noise -- the original noise transformed with the pixel shear-response operator, plus the added noise carrying an assigned shear dependence that we are free to choose -- must be independent of shear to first order. Under this condition the shear response of the renoised ellipticity is estimated from the known realization of the added noise alone. The rotated noise field, which we call rotation renoising, is one solution of the condition and yields the analytical response estimator of AnaCal. We then construct a second solution, spectral renoising, which adds only a small fraction of the original noise variance: for homogeneous Gaussian noise the added field is an independent, scaled-down copy of the image noise, and its assigned shear response is the same field passed through a fixed filter set by the noise power spectrum deconvolved by the point spread function. Image simulations show that spectral renoising keeps the multiplicative shear bias at the $10^{-3}$ level and raises the effective galaxy number density by about 20 per cent at the faint end.

title: The coupled evolution of nuclear star clusters and intermediate-mass black holes in a dwarf-galaxy merger
comment: 23 pages, 14 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to MNRAS. Comments welcome!
summary: Nuclear star clusters (NSCs) and intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) are expected to coexist in low-mass galaxies and might together facilitate the coalescence and growth of IMBHs. We simulate an equal-mass, gas-rich dwarf-galaxy merger in which each progenitor hosts a $10^3\,\rm M_\odot$ IMBH embedded in a $10^6\,\rm M_\odot$ NSC to study their co-evolution. The simulation model combines the multiphase interstellar medium and fully sampled initial stellar mass function of GRIFFIN at $4\,\rm M_\odot$ gas resolution with the regularised post-Newtonian black hole dynamics of KETJU. Black holes are modelled as accreting sink particles without feedback. Without NSCs, $10^3$-$10^4\,\rm M_\odot$ IMBHs sink only to separations of $50$-$200\,\rm pc$ and capture no gas. With NSCs, the clusters coalesce within ${\sim} 500\,\rm Myr$, the IMBHs form a binary within a few Myr, and scattering of mainly old NSC stars drives them to merger ${\sim} 340\,\rm Myr$ later. The NSCs also promote gas capture, growing the black holes to $1.1\times10^5$ and $4.1\times10^4\,\rm M_\odot$. Gas capture is suppressed during the merger-induced starburst by stellar feedback and the motion of the NSCs relative to the gas, and proceeds in brief supernova-regulated episodes once the NSCs have settled in the centre. Scattering by the IMBH binary and the merger recoil of ${\sim} 175\,\rm km\,s^{-1}$, which removes the remnant from the NSC but not from the galaxy, leave a larger, rotating NSC with a flat core. The stellar tidal disruption rate rises towards coalescence, and the merger is detectable with LISA out to high redshift. NSCs thus remove the delivery and hardening bottlenecks of IMBH mergers in low-mass galaxies.

title: The Effective Field Theory Origin of the Fuzzy Sphere Method
comment: 5 pages + references + a page of End Matter + 15 pages of Supplemental Materials; 3 figures
summary: Fuzzy sphere Hamiltonians for (2+1)D conformal field theories are usually written directly on the lowest Landau level. We introduce a framework organizing them as descendants of local ``mother theories'' on $S^2\times\mathbb R$. We start with the example of Ising mother theory built from two charged Dirac fermions coupled to a real mediator $φ$. Integrating out $φ$ and the higher Landau levels produces the fuzzy Hamiltonian, while integrating out the fermions gives a conventional local $φ$ effective field theory flowing to the Ising point. Mild modifications of the same theory reach the Gaussian point (tricritical route) and the Lee-Yang continuation. Exploring the space of mother theories, we next promote $φ$ to a complex field $Φ$ and construct a new example, whose descendant is an easy-plane ferromagnet on the fuzzy sphere. Its spontaneous symmetry breaking phase gives a pseudo-Goldstone relativistic scalar, similar to the model introduced by Y.-C. He, while its critical point is non-relativistic, providing the first example of $z=2$ scaling on the fuzzy sphere. Remarkably, it admits exact one-magnon solutions, and the $z=2$ critical point can be found analytically. We then outline a rich landscape of further applications of our approach.

title: Preparation of a celestial field for precise VLBI observations of the JUICE spacecraft: a test case of the Venus flyby
comment: 13 pages, 6 tables, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in PASA
summary: The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer mission, launched in 2023, is on its way to the Jovian system, to arrive in 2031. The Planetary Radio Interferometry and Doppler Experiment performs radio astronomical observations of the spacecraft already in its interplanetary cruise phase. Since the sky density of potential compact radio sources suitable as phase-reference calibrators in very long baseline interferometry observations is low, densifying the celestial reference frame along the Ecliptic is an essential task in support of JUICE. In preparation for the JUICE gravity assist manoeuvre at Venus in August 2025, to support the accurate reconstruction of the spacecraft state vector, we selected in-beam calibrator source candidates along the JUICE trajectory. Additionally, we attempted to link known nearby bright compact reference sources from the Radio Fundamental Catalog to the International Celestial Reference Frame. We performed nodding-style phase-referencing VLBI observations with the European VLBI Network at 8.4GHz, targeting nine in-beam calibrator candidate and three RFC sources in the celestial vicinity of JUICE's trajectory during its Venus flyby. We linked their positions to nearby ICRF sources by means of relative astrometry. Four of the ICC targets and all RFC sources were detected and imaged with the EVN, and their coordinates determined with typically sub-mas precision. Although none of the targeted ICC sources proved suitable as VLBI phase-reference calibrators because of being too faint or resolved, their newly-determined positions and flux densities could in principle be used to verify the detection of the spacecraft at the time of the actual flyby around Venus. During the detailed analysis of the ICC targets, we found that the structure of one of them, J0843+1826 is resolved on mas scale, and the other one, J0843+1814 is a young radio galaxy, likely a member of a cluster.

title: Quantum Observables of Nonperturbative Superradiant Scattering
summary: Inelastic scattering from $N$ coherent spins, or any two-state system, scales as $N^2$, invalidating the Born approximation at large $N$ even at weak coupling. We develop a nonperturbative theory of this superradiant scattering and its backreaction on the spins. Since one particle can exchange many quanta, the target's energy-transfer and energy-variance rates keep their favorable $N^2$ scaling even after the cross section saturates, unless a conservation law limits each encounter to exchange of one quantum. We apply the theory to millicharged-particle searches, as well as neutron and charged-particle beams that can test quantum protocols for detecting cosmic relics.

title: Isospectrality breaking in the axial quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity
summary: We study odd-parity perturbations of Reissner-Nordström black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity. The dCS action is parity invariant because $\vartheta\,{}^{*}RR$ is the product of two pseudoscalars; nevertheless, the pseudoscalar perturbation has odd parity and enters only the axial sector at linear order and so lifts the axial--polar isospectrality of general relativity. We derive the finite-charge couplings between the pseudoscalar and the axial gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations directly from the linearized field equations. Both directions are governed by the radial kernel $(Mr-Q^2)Δ/r^8$, and at nonzero charge the pseudoscalar couples to $Ψ+χΨ_e$, with $χ=2Q/[r\sqrt{(l-1)(l+2)}]$. After diagonalizing the Einstein--Maxwell sector, we compute branch-resolved quasinormal-mode shifts with exterior complex scaling for the photon-sphere modes and Frobenius shooting for the near-extremal zero-damping modes. For the Schwarzschild $l=2$ fundamental mode we obtain $β\,δω=-0.7733-0.3946\,i$ (units $M=α=1$). Off resonance, the gravitational-led shift scales as $ζ\,l^3$ at $Q=0$ but as $ζ\,l^2/Q$ at fixed nonzero charge and large $l$. The electromagnetic-led branch becomes exactly degenerate with the pseudoscalar mode at $Q_c=2M\sqrt{l(l+1)+1}/[l(l+1)+2]$, where the pseudoscalar potential coincides with the polar partner of the electromagnetic-led potential; there the breaking is $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtζ)$, $M|Δω|\simeq2.4\sqrtζ$ for $l=2$, and the shift reverses sign across $Q_c$. Near extremality the photon-sphere shifts remain finite, whereas the non-degenerate fundamental gravitational-led zero-damping mode is suppressed, $δω/ω\simeq6.0\times10^{3}\,ζ\,(1-Q^2/M^2)$ for $l=2$.

title: Cosmological constraints on extra radiation and early dark energy with lepton asymmetry and varying quark masses
summary: We investigate cosmological constraints on extra radiation and axionlike early dark energy (EDE), allowing primordial lepton asymmetry or light-quark-mass variation during big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). We combine Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ supernovae, and primordial helium and deuterium measurements. When both extra radiation and lepton asymmetry are allowed, we obtain $N_{\rm eff}=3.27\pm0.16$, $ξ=0.017\pm0.011$, and $H_0=69.24\pm0.92\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. A positive lepton asymmetry compensates the helium increase caused by extra radiation, allowing a higher inferred Hubble constant even with the LBT helium measurement, which agrees with standard BBN. For EDE, primordial-abundance measurements instead restrict the higher baryon densities associated with larger EDE fractions, which reduce the predicted deuterium abundance. Allowing lepton asymmetry does not relax this restriction. In contrast, a positive light-quark-mass variation increases deuterium and compensates this reduction, permitting larger EDE fractions and a higher inferred Hubble constant. The same variation leaves the extra-radiation constraint nearly unchanged. We also find that allowing lepton asymmetry relaxes the 95\% upper limit on the summed neutrino mass from $0.0640\,{\rm eV}$ to $0.0777\,{\rm eV}$ in the extra-radiation model.

title: ARRAKIHS: The observability of tidally stripped satellites in a Milky Way-like halo
comment: 16 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: Deep imaging surveys are revealing increasing numbers of low surface brightness stellar streams around Milky Way-like galaxies. These streams trace the orbital evolution and internal structure of their disrupted dwarf galaxy progenitors. We investigate the evolution and observability of tidal features from dwarf galaxies consistent with the $Λ$CDM framework and Local Group observations. We performed high-resolution $N$-body simulations of dwarf galaxies orbiting in a static Milky Way-like potential comprising a disc, bulge, and dark matter halo. Each dwarf comprised a Plummer stellar distribution embedded in a cuspy or cored generalised Navarro--Frenk--White dark matter halo. Idealised integrated surface brightness maps were constructed every 0.5 Gyr over 10 Gyr, and detectability was quantified through the projected area of stellar light brighter than limiting surface brightnesses, $μ_{\rm lim}=29$--$32$ mag arcsec$^{-2}$, chosen to span depths relevant to ARRAKIHS, LSST, and Euclid. The detectability of tidal features depends most strongly on progenitor stellar mass, orbital configuration, parameterised by the eccentricity proxy $e_0$, and evolutionary stage. Across this range, extended tidal debris is predominantly recovered for initially more radial configurations, mainly those with $e_0 \gtrsim 0.75$. In the simulated grid, detectable area is dominated by $M_\star=10^8$--$10^9 M_\odot$ progenitors, whereas $M_\star=10^6$--$10^7 M_\odot$ systems can undergo stripping without detectable debris. The detectable area evolves non-monotonically with time, reflecting the competition between stream formation, phase mixing, and the fading of diffuse debris below the adopted surface brightness limits. Cuspy and cored progenitors show similar evolution of the detectable area, with differences smaller than the scatter induced by orbital diversity.

title: Unifying energy-entropy bounds in semiclassical gravity
summary: We revisit bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity, aiming to strengthen and unify established bounds, in particular the quantum focussing conjecture (QFC) and the smeared null energy condition (SNEC). Both the QFC and SNEC have important applications and are the strongest in their respective hierarchies; however, neither implies the other, nor reduces to the null energy condition (NEC) in the classical limit. To that end, we define a new class of bounds dubbed gravitational energy-entropy conditions (GEECs) that imply both the QFC and SNEC, and reduce to the NEC classically. We construct an explicit family of GEECs by imposing the defining criteria on a broad set of stress tensor bounds, and constrain its remaining parameter space through test cases, in an effective field theory-inspired approach. Our GEECs are powerful candidate bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity.

title: Identifying narrow-band mutual coupling resonances in SKA-low stations using frequency-independent current basis functions
summary: Mutual coupling between closely spaced elements in aperture arrays introduces narrow-band spectral features in the Embedded Element Patterns (EEPs), threatening measurements of the 21-cm power spectrum with instruments such as SKA-low. We detail a method to identify such features through the construction of frequency-independent current basis functions, utilising a singular value decomposition of frequency-dependent basis functions. We demonstrate the method on a three-element linear array and full pseudo-random station of SKA log-periodic antennas and examine the current power induced by mutual coupling. For the pseudo-random layout station we note many narrow-band resonance features, including strong resonances at 50.8~MHz and 83.6~MHz, where the coupled power on the passive antennas can approach or exceed that of the excited antenna. Simulated delay power spectra for the SKA-low core show that observing in frequency bands including resonance features causes large foreground leakage within the delay power spectra, obscuring the EoR window. For the pseudo-random layout station with SKALA4.0 we identify two significant frequency bands from 59.2--76.2~MHz and 84.2--103.3~MHz which are free of contamination from current resonances, preserving the EoR window in these frequency ranges.

title: How natural are Froggatt-Nielsen Models?
summary: The Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) mechanism aims at a natural explanation of the surprising hierarchical structure of the masses and mixings of Standard Model quarks and leptons. We test this claimed naturalness against various known and some original measures of fine-tuning, including various local measures as well as Bayes fac- tors. The FN models serve as a fruitful laboratory for testing and comparing these measures. We find that the standard Barbieri-Giudice metric is overestimating nat- uralness in many cases, as it does not sufficiently account for the failure of a model to be realized at order-one parameter values, even though the latter are favoured by an appropriate prior distribution. As a side product of our study, we present simple geometric expressions for the posterior distributions of the parameters on the manifold of best-fit values.

title: Bosonic Dark Matter Cores Can Screen Scalar-Tensor Gravity
summary: We examine the observational viability of scalarized fermion-boson stars (FBSs) in massless Damour-Esposito-Farèse gravity, using the MPA1 nuclear equation of state and a self-interacting complex scalar field playing the role of an ultralight bosonic dark matter model. Constraining stellar models within a multi-messenger-motivated mass-radius window, we obtain three main results: First, bosonic dark matter acts as a catalyst for spontaneous scalarization. Second, energetically favored configurations are scalarized FBSs featuring bosonic dark matter cores that reconcile strongly coupled regimes with radius bounds. Third, dark matter cores tend to suppress scalar charges, which mimics the effect of a massive gravitational scalar field and could contribute to evade observational constraints. Additionally, the exclusive prediction of scalarized FBSs at high masses suggests a way to test this theoretical scenario.

title: Efficient GLS map-making and assessment of $1/f$ noise impact for future CMB satellite missions
comment: 25 pages + appendix and bibliography, 17 figures, 4 tables
summary: Time-correlated $1/f$ noise is a major source of large-scale contamination in measurements of the polarized cosmic microwave background (CMB) that can limit sensitivity to primordial $B$ modes. Generalized least-squares (GLS) map-making is optimal for stationary Gaussian noise when its covariance is known, but practical implementations rely on approximations to make the computation tractable. In particular, approximating the noise covariance as circulant enables efficient map-making using fast Fourier transform, but introduces artificial edge effects when applied to finite data chunks. We introduce STITCH (STatistical Inpainting for Timeline CHunks), a preprocessing method that mitigates these effects by extending time-ordered data chunks with synthetic samples that make the extended timelines statistically consistent with the assumed circulant noise model. They can then be processed with standard circulant GLS solvers, preserving their computational efficiency while reducing residuals associated with chunk boundaries. Simulations show that STITCH substantially suppresses these edge effects, bringing the resulting noise power spectra close to those obtained when the circulant approximation holds. We demonstrate negligible impact of our procedure on the recovered signal, such as $E\to B$ leakage, even at large scales. Finally, we investigate how temporal $1/f$ noise projects onto angular scales for representative LiteBIRD-, \emph{Planck}-, and PICO-like scanning strategies. Using noise simulations spanning a range of temporal noise parameters, we fit an effective model to the resulting angular noise spectra. These results provide an empirical characterization of the temporal-to-angular noise mapping for the configurations studied and a basis for further investigations of correlated noise in future CMB polarization missions.

title: The extragalactic science of the KMOS VVVX-GalCen spectroscopic survey II: Discovery of a galaxy cluster at z = 0.089 behind the Galactic plane
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures. Letter accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The Zone of Avoidance (ZoA) continues to represent the most significant incompleteness in the extragalactic census of the Local Universe. It is evident that photometric surveys alone are insufficient to establish whether the galaxy overdensities detected therein are physical systems or projections along the line of sight. We present the first spectroscopic results of the extragalactic science area of the KMOS VVVX-GalCen Spectroscopic Survey, demonstrating how near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy can reveal and dynamically characterise galaxy clusters hidden by the Milky Way. A photometric overdensity of 19 galaxy candidates was identified in the VVV NIRGC III catalogue, centred at $(l,b)=(274.05^\circ,+2.85^\circ)$ with a mean interstellar extinction of $A_{K_s}=0.2$ mag; 16 of these candidates were observed with VLT/KMOS in the $HK$ grating and yielded spectra with reliable cross-correlation radial velocities. A total of 14 galaxies form a compact structure with a mean redshift of $\langle z \rangle = 0.089 \pm 0.001$, which corresponds to a mean radial velocity $\langle cz \rangle = 26660 \pm 170$ km/s, while two are foreground galaxies. The rest-frame line-of-sight velocity dispersion is $σ_v = 560^{+110}_{-120}$ km/s, implying an indicative dynamical mass of $M_{200} = 1.9^{+0.7}_{-1.1} \times 10^{14} M_\odot$ (based on members within the cluster core $\sim 0.4 r_{200}$) and placing the system in the poor-cluster regime. Of these 14 cluster members, 13 also lie within the $2σ$ scatter of the fitted near-IR red sequence. The other two galaxies are foreground objects that lie outside this range.

title: Collective Bootstrap for Matrix Quantum Mechanics
summary: We develop a collective bootstrap framework for large $N$ matrix quantum mechanics formulated directly in the loop space of single trace coordinate moments. Loop joining and splitting operations organize the kinetic constraints systematically and avoid treating momentum containing moments as independent variables. Employing the virial theorem, a Schur complement, and a relaxation of quadratic products of loops, we recast the nonlinear constrained optimization of the collective energy into a semidefinite program, which yields a lower bound on the planar ground state energy at every truncation. A sequential semidefinite optimization heuristic then searches for configurations satisfying planar factorization and estimates the ground state energy and loop expectation values. Applications to one-, two-, and three-matrix models exhibit close agreement with analytic solutions and master field optimization. By working exclusively with coordinate moments, the framework permits truncations at higher word length and offers a promising approach to models with more matrices, including the bosonic sectors of the BFSS and BMN models.

title: Temporal regularization of petal modes in SCAO systems: The Soft-Limiter approach
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. 13 pages, 9 figures
summary: Extremely large telescopes (ELTs) rely on segmented mirrors and thick support structures that fragment the pupil. In single-conjugate AO (SCAO), this produces differential pistons, or petal modes. The Pyramid Wavefront Sensor (PWFS), baseline for ANDES, MICADO, HARMONI, and GMT-NGSAO, has poor sensitivity to these modes in the visible under realistic residual turbulence. We aim to prevent the "Island Effect", where poorly observed differential pistons accumulate and degrade the PSF, without compromising continuous-mode correction. We propose the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) Soft-Limiter, a deterministic, lightweight controller combining a subspace MMSE estimator derived from von Kármán priors with a continuous temporal regularization. It acts as a leaky integrator applied only to the relative petal degrees of freedom. End-to-end SPECULA simulations of ELT/ANDES show that, while a classical integrator loses lock and wanders across multiple fringes at seeing $\ge 1.0''$, the MMSE Soft-Limiter confines the differential piston within a single fringe over the $0.6-1.2''$ range. It bounds the petal excursion and its science-band impact under severe turbulence, while keeping optimal continuous-mode correction at good seeing, without the Strehl penalty of spatial mitigation such as Edge Actuator Coupling. We derive and verify the operating window for the leakage gain, $g \lesssim g_{\mathrm{eff}}/π$: below it, the fast loop retains genuine physical steps up to $λ_{WFS}/2$ with a small droop. This maintains a stable modulo-$λ_{WFS}$ wavefront on the fast sensor, letting a slower phasing sensor resolve integer ambiguities. As the window narrows with turbulence, its boundaries cross near $1.0''$ seeing; beyond this, retaining physical discontinuities becomes the sole responsibility of the phasing channel, a key design driver for segmented ELTs.

title: Positive-weight moment matching at NNLO and beyond
summary: Parton-shower simulations at state-of-the-art perturbative accuracy carry many negative event weights, which dilute their statistical power. For many purposes, this makes them unusable. We formulate a method for the generation of positive-weighted event samples which reproduce, up to a controllable approximation, suites of IR-safe observables with the highest perturbative accuracy of any available calculation. This method is arbitrarily differential in phase space, and free from unphysical artefacts such as binning-dependence. Applied to a leading-order Pythia sample, the method gives simultaneous NNLO accuracy for Drell--Yan and $Z+\text{jet}$ observables in a positive-weighted event sample, for the first time. The method generalises immediately to higher orders of perturbation theory, higher multiplicities, and other processes, observables, and event generators.

title: Fermion-Boson Stars in Scalar-Tensor Gravity
summary: In the massless Damour-Esposito-Farèse scalar-tensor theory of gravity, we numerically construct static, spherically symmetric star models composed of a mixture of fermionic and bosonic matter, interacting purely gravitationally. The fermionic sector is modeled as a perfect fluid, while the bosonic sector is described by a massive, free, complex scalar field. We demonstrate that mixed fermion-boson stars can undergo spontaneous scalarization, and we systematically investigate the role played by the bosonic field across different regimes of bosonic mass, central fermionic pressure, and central bosonic amplitude. Our analysis reveals a complex interplay among the parameters, giving rise to a variety of scalarized configurations, ranging from fermionic matter embedded within extended bosonic halos to bosonic cores confined within fermionic matter. We examine sequences of solutions, in particular mass-radius surfaces, and we determine the critical coupling parameter for the onset of scalarization.

title: Dwarf Galaxy Reticulum II's MeerKAT L-Band Observation: Constraining WIMP Dark Matter
summary: The nature of dark matter remains one of the most profound open questions in modern physics, with weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) among the leading candidates proposed to account for the observed anomalies across cosmic scales. If WIMPs annihilate or decay in the dense dark matter haloes of nearby galaxies, the resulting high-energy electrons/positrons can produce synchrotron radiation in the presence of ambient magnetic fields, yielding a potentially detectable radio signature. Dwarf spheroidal galaxies are particularly promising targets for indirect dark matter searches due to their high mass-to-light ratios and low astrophysical foreground contamination. While radio observations have been widely used to constrain WIMP properties in these systems, the resulting limits remain highly sensitive to poorly constrained magnetic field assumptions. Here we utilize L-band ($1.3$--$1.5$ GHz) observations from the MeerKAT array directed towards dwarf galaxy Reticulum II and measure the surface brightness profile across the dwarf galaxy. Combining these measurements with theoretical models of WIMP annihilation and yield 95% confidence level upper limits on the WIMP annihilation cross-section $\langleσv\rangle \lesssim 10^{-26}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ for masses $m_χ\sim 10$-$200$ GeV (with the assumed uniform magnetic field model and diffusion constant). As next-generation radio facilities such as the Square Kilometre Array come online, robust characterisation of magnetic environments in dwarf galaxies will be essential to fully exploit their sensitivity to the particle nature of dark matter.

title: Environmental Quenching of Satellite Galaxies out to z~0.4 with GAMA and DEVILS
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: While numerous studies have shown that satellite galaxies experience declining star formation rates after infall, direct comparisons across different surveys and redshifts are complicated by varying sample selections, environmental metrics, and techniques used to derive galaxy properties. In this work, we select satellite galaxies from the highly complete Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) Survey and the Deep Extragalactic VIsible Legacy Survey (DEVILS) to investigate environmental quenching out to z~0.4. These surveys derive galaxy properties and environments in a consistent manner, minimizing systematic biases and enabling a robust comparison across redshift. Using projected phase space as a proxy for infall time, we quantify the evolution of the quenched fraction and trace how satellites evolve relative to the star-forming main sequence (SFMS). We find consistent trends between GAMA and DEVILS, with satellites exhibiting a steady decline in star formation relative to the SFMS at a rate of ~0.14 dex/Gyr following infall. Extending this analysis to include visual morphology, we find similar declining trends for both early- and late-type systems. Overall, we find no significant redshift evolution between GAMA and DEVILS, indicating that group and cluster environments have a comparable impact on the star formation activity of satellite galaxies over the past ~4.5 Gyr.

title: Elliptic master integrals and the one-loop cosmological wavefunction
summary: Loop corrections to the cosmological wavefunction involve similar integrals to those required for scattering amplitudes. For the one-loop triangle of a conformally coupled scalar, the master integrals are elliptic, and so the triangle wavefunction coefficient was expected to be elliptic as well. Using a bootstrap approach, we compute this triangle coefficient exactly and show that it is not: the elliptic periods cancel, and the flat-space wavefunction coefficient is a combination of dilogarithms. The cancellation occurs because the residue of the loop integrand on the elliptic sector is a flat-space amplitude, rational in the loop momentum. The one-loop box, by contrast, is not polylogarithmic, even with a single external leg at each site. Its threshold discontinuity involves elliptic integrals, which we also give in closed form. For regular-tetrahedron momenta the periods of a K3 surface enter its loop integrand.

title: Model-Based Retrieval of Four Years of JWST/NIRCam Wavefronts
summary: The fidelity of data recovered by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) depends on precise monitoring of the mirror segments' surfaces and alignment. To this end, every few days the observatory takes pairs of defocused images of a reference star with its NIRCam instrument; a closed-source phase retrieval package is then employed to infer the wavefront. We here present camino (Computational Aberration Modelling and Inference for NIRCam Observations), an open-source algorithm to model NIRCam built in JAX using the differentiable Fresnel optics code dLUX and regularised maximum likelihood inference that has been conditioned on the entire archive of NIRCam wavefront sensing data. We typically improve the reduced chi-squared in fits to the defocused data from 60-65 to 12-13. We reconstruct the wavefront history of JWST from the beginning of science operations to early 2026. This open source implementation operates in parallel to the current STScI phase retrieval algorithm, allowing access by the broader scientific community to high-accuracy wavefront estimation and enabling its direct integration into science-analysis workflows. This represents a major step towards the ultimate goal of predictive calibration methods based on physics-based forward modelling, obviating the need for time-consuming observation of contemporaneous dedicated reference stars.

title: Neutrino electromagnetic properties after the first $pp$ solar neutrino observation at XENONnT
summary: The XENONnT Collaboration has recently reported the first measurement of low-energy solar neutrinos through elastic neutrino-electron scattering in a dark matter detector, opening a new window on Standard Model predictions and on neutrino electromagnetic properties. We analyze these data to extract the $pp$ neutrino flux normalization and the weak mixing angle at low momentum transfer ($\sim 0.1$ MeV). We also derive bounds on the neutrino charge radii, magnetic moments, and millicharges, as well as on the sterile-neutrino dipole portal. Since the $pp$-flux determination displays a mild excess, we further investigate the role of the $^{14}$C background in the fit and assess how it affects the extracted parameters. Our results show that dark matter detectors now offer a probe of neutrino physics that is complementary to dedicated precision experiments.

title: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background
summary: The stochastic gravitational-wave background from stellar-mass compact binaries is non-Gaussian since it is made up of a finite number of individual mergers. Over the years, several methods have been developed to search for this background beyond the standard cross-correlation statistic. We reformulate the data analysis problem for such astrophysical backgrounds in terms of the characteristic function of the data in multiple detectors, and show that the existing searches arise as different limiting cases. We also show that new searches can be constructed through different approximations of the characteristic function, which gives a concrete way to engineer suitable approximate sufficient statistics. To illustrate this framework in the context of a simple example, we use the formalism proposed here to analyze an exactly solvable toy model.

title: Mapping cluster angular momentum with the rotational kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect
summary: Galaxy clusters carry angular momentum. If the intracluster gas rotates coherently, the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect imprints a dipole on the microwave sky centered on the cluster. We show that microwave maps alone can be used to reconstruct a noisy vector field tracing the projected angular momentum of the ionized gas. We present an optimal multifrequency matched filter (MMF) that isolates the rotational kSZ (rkSZ) signal from the much larger miscentered thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect, cosmic microwave, and infrared background contributions, improving on both real-space oriented stacking and matched filtering of maps cleaned with full-sky multifrequency weights. For the rkSZ profile, we introduce a simple model for coherent intracluster gas rotation and validate it against TNG-Cluster and TNG300-1. The model consists of differentially rotating concentric shells with constant equatorial tangential velocity, characterized by a mass- and redshift-indepedent tangential-to-circular velocity ratio of $v_{\rm tan}/V_{c,200c}=0.18$. Using this model, we forecast single-cluster signal-to-noise (SNR) as a function of mass and redshift for Simons Observatory; cross-correlation with an external catalog of rotation proxies yields a cumulative detection SNR. For an idealized mass-limited catalog with perfectly known spin directions, the cumulative SNR of our optimal MMF reaches $\approx 53$, $25$, and $6$ when including all clusters above $\log_{10}(M_{200c}/M_\odot)>14$, 14.5, and 15, respectively. This work provides a practical framework for CMB measurements of intracluster gas rotation, with applications to the rotational contribution to non-thermal pressure in cluster mass calibration, as well as spin alignments and clustering biases.

title: Odds Estimation for Supermassive Black Hole Binaries in Local Core Galaxies
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables, submitted to AAS Journals
summary: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) are expected products of massive galaxy mergers, but identifying binaries in nearby galaxies remains challenging. We combine simulated massive-galaxy assembly histories from IllustrisTNG with a semi-analytic core-scouring model to connect observable core galaxy properties to the probability of hosting a bound SMBHB at z=0. We (i) construct a core galaxy population using an observationally motivated galaxy stellar mass function, (ii) model binary evolution through dynamical friction, stellar hardening, and gravitational-wave emission, and (iii) perform logistic regressions with five observable predictors: stellar mass deficit, stellar mass, central density, central velocity dispersion, and effective radius. The resulting models perform well on simulated systems, achieving a pseudo-$R^2$ of $0.51\pm0.03$, accuracy $0.95\pm0.01$, precision $0.92\pm0.03$, and recall $0.82\pm0.04$. Uncoalesced binaries are typically compact, with separations peaking near 0.3 pc, though only $\sim0.3\%$ emit in the pulsar timing array band. Applying the model to observed core galaxies, we identify eight nearby galaxies more likely than not to host SMBHBs. Of those eight host candidates, we note Messier 86 (NGC 4406) as a particularly likely example that was similarly identified using independent means and therefore warrants future follow-up.

title: From pq-webs to magnetic quivers and back I: dictionary and deformations
summary:
This is the first of two companion papers in which we study five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories engineered by $(p,q)$ five-brane webs and their associated three-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ magnetic quivers. We focus on the $N+\mathrm{SU}(N)_0^{k-1}+N$ box quiver theories. We propose an exact parameter dictionary relating the five-dimensional flavour masses and instanton couplings to the Fayet-Iliopoulos parameters of the corresponding strong-coupling magnetic quiver.
  We test this dictionary through a broad class of deformations, including mass deformations, weak-coupling limits, and vacuum expectation values. On the five-dimensional side, we implement these flows directly at the level of the superconformal index. The dictionary fixes the corresponding FI deformations and monopole VEVs. We analyse them in the magnetic-quiver squashed-sphere partition function using a new method that tracks Higgsing, decoupled sectors, and infrared theories. Our results promote magnetic quivers to tools for the quantitative study of how the five-dimensional superconformal index responds to deformations. Once the parameter dictionary is known, exact three-dimensional observables can be used to reconstruct the corresponding five-dimensional physics and to navigate the full deformation network in both directions.

title: posterior-landscape: morphological feature finding in two-dimensional probability densities
comment: 15 pages (41 total), 8 figures (10 total). Code available at https://github.com/Mik3M4n/posterior-landscape
summary: We present posterior-landscape, a Python framework to identify and characterize morphological features in two-dimensional probability densities. The framework combines concepts from topological data analysis, statistical density-ridge estimation, and scale-space image analysis. It extracts localized concentrations, valleys, ridges, and changes of slope; for Bayesian reconstructions, it propagates uncertainty in feature recovery, geometry, and correspondence across posteriors. The framework also connects two-dimensional structures to features in one-dimensional marginals, and quantifies their correlation with other inferred parameters. We validate the method on controlled densities, and demonstrate its use on gravitational-wave population reconstructions, where it provides a systematic way to identify and interpret population features and assess which ones carry information relevant for cosmology. The resulting catalogues also offer a common morphological representation for future comparisons between predictions and population reconstructions.

title: Searching for Dark Photons and ALPs using Gamma-rays from Nuclear Reactors
summary: Nuclear reactors are intense sources of MeV gamma rays, produced in fission, radiative neutron capture and the de-excitation of fission products. Building on earlier phenomenological studies, we present a detector-independent description of the production of light, weakly coupled particles by reactor gamma rays and of their detection through scattering, absorption and decay in a nearby detector. We consider kinetically mixed dark photons, produced and detected through Compton-like processes, and axion-like particles (ALPs) coupled to photons, electrons and nucleons, produced through Primakoff conversion, Compton-like scattering and magnetic nuclear transitions such as the $2.23~\mathrm{MeV}$ line of $p(n,γ)d$. As a concrete application, we derive the projected sensitivities of the CONUS+ germanium experiment at the Leibstadt reactor and of a conceivable $100$-kg CONUS100 upgrade. For sub-MeV dark photons, CONUS+ and CONUS100 reach kinetic mixings of $ε\simeq1.65\times10^{-5}$ and $1.2\times10^{-5}$, respectively, for $0.5~\mathrm{keV}\lesssim m_{A'}\lesssim0.5~\mathrm{MeV}$. For ALPs, we show that CONUS100 can probe an unexplored region of parameter space at MeV masses, in particular through $a\to e^+e^-$ decays of ALPs emitted in the deuteron line, assuming a energy window extended to $10~\mathrm{MeV}$.

title: Unifying stochastic and deterministic signals: a practical search for the intermittent binary black-hole background
summary: Over the past decade, the Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA detectors have detected nearly 400 compact binary mergers, most of which are stellar-mass binary black-hole (BBH) mergers. Nevertheless, most mergers in the Universe are too weak to be individually detected at current sensitivity levels. Since a BBH merger in band is much shorter than the average time between successive mergers, the population of these subthreshold events gives rise to an intermittent background of gravitational waves (GWs). This GW background is guaranteed to exist, but it has not yet been detected with current stochastic or deterministic searches. Here we propose a fast and accurate likelihood-based search for this background, which unifies the standard model-agnostic cross-correlation search and a fully deterministic, template-based search in a single likelihood. Our search is based on a truncated likelihood ratio, which is fully marginalized over the extrinsic parameters of the individual mergers, and which represents the data in two detectors as an expansion in terms of approximate sufficient statistics. These statistics are higher-order cross-moments of the data, weighted by geometrical factors that generalize the standard overlap reduction function (ORF) used in cross-correlation searches. We show that almost all the Bayesian evidence and information on the BBH merger population comes from correlations between frequency bins induced by individual mergers and is captured in the higher-order generalized ORFs. Consequently, any likelihood function that does not take these inter-frequency correlations into account is necessarily suboptimal. We validate our search on one year of simulated Advanced LIGO data, and find that a catalog-informed analysis, which uses information from both the detected and unresolved mergers, can infer the peak of the redshift distribution of the population of BBH mergers.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Neural Networks Developed for MBHB Coalescence in the Context of LISA Space Mission
comment: Submitted to Classical and Quantum Gravity
summary: Machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly explored to analyse gravitational wave (GW) data expected from the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). At the same time, advances in quantum computing have stimulated interest in quantum machine learning as a potential alternative to conventional approaches. We investigate the applicability of quantum, hybrid quantum-classical, and classical ML models to two tasks relevant for LISA observations of massive black hole binaries: GW signal detection and merger prediction. Using the Sangria dataset from the LISA Data Challenge, we benchmark several quantum architectures, including variational quantum classifiers (VQCs), post VQC hybrid models, quantum kernel methods, data reuploading classifiers, and quantum long short-term memory (QLSTM) networks, against classical support vector machines, multilayer perceptrons, recurrent neural networks, and LSTM networks. The models are trained on labelled data derived from the Sangria training dataset and evaluated on the corresponding blind dataset. For signal detection, several quantum models match or outperform classical baselines. In particular, the best performing hybrid post VQC architecture correctly identifies all signal samples in the blind dataset, while the standard VQC and data reuploading classifier achieve competitive detection rates. For merger detection and coalescence time estimation, however, the standard VQC emerges as the most reliable model, successfully localising all detected merger events with the lowest localisation errors. We further analyse the trade-offs between predictive performance, model complexity, and quantum circuit resources. Our results indicate that, although no universal quantum advantage is observed, selected quantum models can provide practical benefits for specific GW analysis tasks and represent promising candidates for future LISA data analysis pipelines.

title: Detailed chemo-dynamical characterization of four elusive Milky Way star clusters
summary: A variety of faint and observationally challenging stellar systems has been discovered in the Milky Way in the last decades. Unveiling their kinematic and chemical properties is crucial to understand their nature and to assess their role in the history of our Galaxy. In this paper, we present a chemo-dynamical analysis of four elusive stellar systems (BH 140, Garro 01, BLISS 1, and Kim 3) using spectra collected with the X-shooter medium-resolution spectrograph at the VLT. We derived precise line-of-sight velocities and chemical abundances for all targets. Specifically, we provide the first spectroscopic characterization of metallicity and α-element content for BH 140, the first comprehensive chemical characterization for BLISS 1 and Garro 01, and the first spectroscopic metallicity determination for Kim 3. BH 140, Garro 01 and BLISS 1 are relatively metal-rich systems with [Fe/H] ~ -0.7 dex and have enhanced α-element abundances, whereas Kim 3 is notably metal-poor with [Fe/H] ~ -1.8 dex. We also performed an orbital analysis to investigate their origin as accreted or in situ systems. We found that Garro 01 and BH 140 have orbits confined within < 1.5 kpc from the Galactic plane, the former having also a remarkably circular orbit. They were likely born in situ, although the high orbital eccentricity of BH 140 and its mild deficiency in α-elements leave other possibilities open. Although undoubtedly accreted, BLISS 1 does not exhibit a clear dynamical association with any known progenitor, lying in a high energy (E) - high vertical angular momentum (LZ ) prograde orbit reaching a maximum height from the Galactic plane of zmax ~ 8 kpc. Its chemical properties seem to favor an in situ origin, which might be connected with the Aleph sub-structure. Finally, we tentatively link the high energy and low LZ orbit of Kim 3 to the Elqui stream.

title: From pq-webs to magnetic quivers and back II: distributional indices and 5d theories breaking bad
summary: This is the second of two companion papers in which we study five-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories engineered by $(p,q)$ five-brane webs and their associated three-dimensional magnetic quivers. Leveraging the exact parameter dictionary between the $N+\mathrm{SU}(N)_0^{k-1}+N$ theories and their magnetic quivers at infinite coupling, proposed in the first paper, we investigate nilpotent moment-map VEV deformations and their three-dimensional counterparts. We show that, when the Higgsing is excessive, the five-dimensional superconformal index becomes distributional, mirroring a characteristic feature of bad and broken theories in three dimensions. We also develop a five-brane web interpretation of these results, identifying the Hanany-Witten moves associated with the Higgsing cascade and relating inequivalent frames to distinct tessellations of the generalised toric diagram.

title: Measuring Precipitable Water Vapor through Dual-Band GPS at Rubin Observatory
comment: 25 pages, 15 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to PASP
summary: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) in Earth's atmosphere is a known source of systematic error in ground-based astronomical measurements, particularly at wavelengths greater than 7,000 angstroms. PWV produces wavelength-dependent extinction in the spectral energy distributions of observed sources. For high-precision applications, such as supernova cosmology, the transmission function must be measured accurately and precisely for each observation. The Vera C. Rubin Observatory is located in the Chilean Andes, a region known for dry conditions. However, even at this location, time-variable absorption by water vapor is a factor. Signal delays from Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) offer a robust, easy, 24-hour monitoring of PWV. In this paper we present measurements from the first six months of GNSS-PWV at Rubin Observatory. We verified our analysis by replicating results from the International GNSS Service (IGS), demonstrating high consistency. We then installed and commissioned a Trimble Net R9 receiver at Allegheny Observatory for a commissioning run before it was relocated to Rubin Observatory. At Rubin Observatory we have been continuously measuring PWV since 2025 September 5. We find average PWV levels of 3.0 kg/m$^2$ in Southern Hemisphere spring (September to November) and 5.4 kg/m$^2$ in summer (December to February). The PWV at Rubin also has a clear daily variation with an amplitude of 1.2-3.8 kg/m$^2$ that is highly correlated with the east-west wind strength. We conclude that the proposed GNSS-based processing method achieves an accuracy of 0.9 kg/m$^2$ with 0.36 kg/m$^2$ precision, confirming the capability for continuous, high-temporal-resolution PWV monitoring to support demanding LSST science cases.

title: Predicting $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ states from a reanalysis of lattice QCD data
summary: We reanalyze the lattice QCD data for the isoscalar $\bar b\bar c ud$ systems with $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ at $m_π\simeq 220$ MeV, incorporating both short- and long-range interactions constrained by heavy-quark spin and chiral symmetries. Using the interaction fitted to the lattice results, we predict a spectrum of isoscalar $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ molecular states with quantum numbers $J^P=0^+$, $1^+$, and $2^+$. The predicted $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $B\bar D$ and $B^*\bar D$ bound states are consistent with the lattice results. Furthermore, the two resonances reported by the lattice collaboration in the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ $\bar b\bar c ud$ channels can be naturally interpreted as $B^*\bar D{}^*$ and $B\bar D{}^*$ hadronic molecules, respectively. We also predict two previously unreported $B^*\bar D{}^*$ states with $J^P=1^+$ and $2^+$: a bound state and a shallow state whose pole may correspond to either a virtual state or a bound state, respectively. Our results provide a unified interpretation of the lattice spectrum and highlight the interplay between short- and long-range interactions in the dynamics of the $B^{(*)}\bar D{}^{(*)}$ systems.

title: The General-Relativistic Limit of f(R) Gravity
summary: We establish the general-relativistic limit of f(R) gravity coupled to a massless scalar field for small, asymptotically Euclidean, well-prepared Cauchy data near Minkowski spacetime. We prove global existence and future causal geodesic completeness, with uniform estimates for the metric, matter, and rescaled effective field as an admissible family of modified Lagrangians f(R) approaches the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian R. The physical and conformal metrics and the matter field converge to the limiting Einstein-massless-scalar development, uniformly on the entire future spacetime, together with finitely many space and time derivatives. The effective field, defined by a nonlinear reparametrization of the physical scalar curvature, converges to the scalar curvature of the limiting Einstein development. The main analytical difficulty is that the effective-field mass tends to infinity, while its evolution equation becomes an algebraic trace relation. Small field amplitudes may coexist with high-frequency oscillations and comparatively large derivatives, whose quadratic contributions must be controlled uniformly. Using the Euclidean-hyperboloidal foliation method and adapted wave coordinates, we analyze a quasilinear wave-Klein-Gordon system whose nonlinearities do not satisfy the classical null condition. We combine oscillatory estimates, weighted interior and exterior energies, and propagation estimates for the discrepancy from the Einstein trace relation. Quantitative convergence on compact regions and uniform spacetime decay yield global convergence.

title: Phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
summary: Cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. In a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. Here we take seriously the possibility of this time dependence and investigate the phenomenological consequences of such an evolution, comparing the results to the more traditional case of a fixed time independent tension. In particular, for five different time varying models, motivated by different possible forms of evolution of the string tension, we evaluate their Gravitational Wave (GW) contributions as well as their impact on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Performing an MCMC analysis of the models we find there are indeed interesting spectral signatures in the GW emission at frequencies between the current PTA and interferometer data, but the signatures are not unique to these strings, making them hard to pin down using current data. However, we do find cosmic strings with evolving tension fit the GW data as well as other favoured models.

title: 3-Methoxy-1-propanol Rotational Spectroscopy and Radio Astronomical Search toward NGC 6334I
summary: The methoxy functionalized alcohol species methoxymethanol and 2-methoxyethanol have recently been identified toward the MM1 protostellar source in the NGC 6334I massive star-forming region. Here we report measurements of portions of the centimeter, millimeter, and sub-millimeter regions of the rotational spectrum of the most stable conformer of 3-methoxy-1-propanol in order to probe the presence of even larger methoxylated alcohols toward the source. The experimental rotational parameters determined from these spectra were used to simulate the rotational spectrum of 3-methoxy-1-propanol under the physical conditions of the MM1 source and compared to the same ALMA observational dataset of the source in which 2-methoxyethanol was first discovered. No 3-methoxy-1-propanol transitions are identified in the data, and an upper limit on its column density toward the source was determined to be $7.5 \cdot 10^{15} \text{ cm}^{-2}$. When considering the series of these three methoxy alcohols, the decrease in column density going from 2-methoxyethanol to 3-methoxy-1-propanol is consistent with how the column density of 2-methoxyethanol decreases compared to methoxymethanol.

title: Holography and localization in fractional field theory
summary: Fractional field theory is a promising framework wherein to quantize the gravitational interaction but the presence of nonlocal operators can make its handling difficult. With the purpose of easing this problem, we recast the theory as a local dual in two ways. First, we generalize the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension theorem to self-adjoint fractional field theories with multi-scale kinetic terms and nonlocal interactions, taking the example of a scalar field. The latter is reinterpreted as a nonlocal boundary degree of freedom holographically dual to a local theory of two scalars living in a higher-dimensional bulk. However, inclusion of a local non-linear potential is not straightforward. We therefore propose an alternative picture where the nonlocal theory is not extended to a higher-dimensional space but is localized at the price of introducing a continuum of masses. This \emph{spectral localization} allows for a natural implementation of the fakeon prescription and the related classicization procedure, already employed in local theories with higher-derivative and complex ghosts. Applications to fractional quantum gravity and its comparison with quadratic quantum gravity are discussed.

title: Tailoring Infra-Red Filters for Global Mapping of Enceladus' Thermal Environment
summary: We present the results of an initial study into the feasibility and design of the Enceladus Thermal Mapper (ETM) instrument, designed to provide detailed temperature data for Enceladus, an icy moon of Saturn identified by the Cassini Mission as a prime candidate for astrobiological study due to its subsurface ocean and active cryovolcanism. Building on heritage from previous missions including TechDemoSat-1, Mars Climate Sounder, and Lunar Trailblazer, ETM aims to measure temperature variations across Enceladus' surface, including at the poles during the extreme cold of winter, when they can reach as low as 45 K. Where Cassini provided limited high-resolution flyby data of Enceladus due to its Saturn-centric orbit, ETM, in orbit around the icy moon will offer continuous high-resolution thermal mapping with a 384 x 288-pixel sensor, capable of 80 m/pixel resolution from 150 km altitude. This will improve constraints on the Enceladus' global conductive heat loss, and better characterise and contextualise its active South Polar Terrain. To optimise the instrument's filters for thermal emission measurements, a digital model of the filter assembly was developed. This lightweight, low-power instrument is capable of significantly advancing the understanding of Enceladus' geological behaviour and evaluating its potential habitability by providing comprehensive temperature data essential for interpreting its evolution.

title: Hunting for Long-Lived ALPs in Top Events via Displaced Dielectron Pairs at the LHC
summary: A generator-level sensitivity study is presented for long-lived axion-like particles (ALPs) produced in association with top-quark pairs and decaying to displaced electron-positron pairs at the CERN LHC. The prompt objects from the top quark-antiquark system provide independent handles for event selection, allowing the event to be selected independently of the displaced electron pair and extending the search to ALP masses below the dimuon threshold. A search strategy motivated by the CMS detector is developed for ALP masses between 17 MeV and 10 GeV and proper decay lengths between 0.1 mm and 1 m. Expected upper limits at 95% confidence level are computed for $σ(pp\to t\bar t a)\times\mathcal{B}(a\to e^+e^-)$ as a function of the ALP mass and proper decay length. In the most sensitive region of the parameter space considered, values of the cross section times branching fraction of order $10^{-3}$ pb can be probed for an integrated luminosity of 500 fb$^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. These projections do not include detector-level displaced-electron reconstruction or instrumental backgrounds.

title: Integrable singularities obstruct Cauchy horizons and mass inflation
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures. Accepted to Physical Review D
summary: Black-hole interiors with an inner (Cauchy) horizon are unstable through the Poisson-Israel-Ori mass-inflation mechanism, governed by the Dray-'t Hooft-Redmount relation and widely regarded as a dynamical realization of strong cosmic censorship. We show that static, spherically symmetric anisotropic interiors supported by a marginally divergent but integrable density $ρ\sim A/r^2$, with $A>1/(8π)$ and mild screening at finite radius, are incompatible with this mechanism. The compactness $q=m/r$ decreases monotonically from a super-critical central value to $1/2$ at the unique event horizon, producing a strictly positive compactness gap throughout the trapped region and excluding any second zero of the lapse. This gap enters the dynamics quantitatively. (i) Under the null energy condition and a dynamical screening condition, $2m/r$ is non-decreasing along both future null directions of a trapped domain, so the gap propagates under nonlinear spherically symmetric evolution. (ii) For ingoing radiation (generalized Vaidya), the gap bounds the blueshift: the advanced time spent in the gapped region is finite, whereas it diverges at a Cauchy horizon. (iii) For counter-streaming null dust, the radiative part $μ$ of the Misner-Sharp mass obeys exactly $\partial_u\partial_vμ=2\,\partial_uμ\,\partial_vμ/(r|f|)$, of which the DTR relation is the thin-shell form; the in-out coupling $2/(r|f|)$ is uniformly bounded on the interior precisely when the gap is positive. This yields an a priori mass bound and, in the Ori thin-shell model, an e-folding rate bounded by the influx luminosity instead of tending to the inner-horizon surface gravity. Integrable-singularity interiors thus realize a class of sources for which the Poisson-Israel-Ori amplification channel is structurally inoperative in the models in which mass inflation was originally established.

title: Extracting non-Gaussian information of line-intensity maps with weighted skew spectra
summary: The bispectrum of line-intensity maps carries cosmological and astrophysical information beyond the power spectrum, but its large data vector hampers the analysis of survey data. Skew spectra address this by compressing the bispectrum into a handful of power-spectrum-like observables, cross-spectra of the observed field with filtered squares of it. We present the first application of optimally weighted skew spectra to line-intensity mapping of galaxy-hosted emission, where all clustering and shot-noise terms are luminosity weighted and the mean intensity is unknown. We perform idealized real-space Fisher forecasts for a SPHEREx-like survey of H$α$ emission at $0.2 \lesssim z \lesssim 4.6$, in its deep fields and in a noisier all-sky configuration. First, the compression carries over to intensity maps: on perturbative scales and for a fixed redshift evolution of the emitters, four skew spectra, one of them matched to the shot noise, recover the bispectrum constraints on biases, shot noise and cosmological parameters to within a few percent. Second, the joint analysis of the power spectrum and the skew spectra measures the ratios of the second-order biases to the linear bias in each redshift bin. Within a bin the biases are degenerate with the unknown mean intensity, but their ratios are not, so their redshift evolution is measured without a model for the emitters. For emission that depends on halo mass alone, these ratios are determined by luminosity-weighted averages of the halo biases, so their evolution can test the halo-emission connection, including dependence on assembly history or environment. The bias ratios are not accessible to the tree-level real-space power spectrum alone. At $z \lesssim 3$ an all-sky SPHEREx-like configuration can detect departures of order $0.1$ in the bias ratios at $3σ$, while deeper fields perform better in the highest-redshift bins.

title: The origin of UV emission in extremely low-mass satellite galaxies: Insights from Leo T
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Leo T, a Milky Way (MW) satellite, is the lowest-mass gas-rich galaxy known to show recent star formation, making it an excellent laboratory for investigating star formation in the ultraviolet (UV) regime within a low-density, metal-poor environment. We present a far-UV (FUV) study using Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (UVIT) data, aiming to characterize FUV star-forming clusters (SFCs), identify FUV-emitting stars, constrain their properties, and explore star formation in an extremely low-mass, metal-poor galaxy. We examined the galaxy's FUV extent and compared it with the H I distribution. We extracted thirty SFCs and derived their properties, including area, luminosity, and star formation rate (SFR), and compared them with previous studies. FUV-emitting stars and their stellar parameters were identified through cross-matching with catalogs from the Hubble Space Telescope and the Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE). We also estimated the global SFR and star formation efficiencies (SFEs) associated with previously identified CO clouds. The FUV luminosities of the SFCs confirm the absence of massive O and B-type stars in Leo T. The FUV-emitting stellar population consists of main-sequence (MS) stars, blue loop (BL) stars, horizontal branch stars, and emission-line (EM) stars. The upper MS and EM stars are concentrated near the optical center, whereas the lower MS and BL stars are more spatially extended. We find that five out of the six FUV-emitting stars with MUSE spectroscopy are extremely metal-poor ([Fe/H] $\leq$ -3). The (NUV - r) color profile indicates that the UV emission is dominated by stellar populations younger than 1 Gyr out to a radius $\lt$ 185 pc. Despite the recent detection of CO(1-0) emission, no SFCs are associated with the molecular clouds, which exhibit extremely low SFEs. The spatial distribution of the SFCs suggests a directional interaction with the MW.

title: Gravitational Reconstruction in $AdS_{4}$
summary: We reconstruct linearized gravitational perturbations in $AdS_{4}$ from a conserved, traceless stress tensor on a fixed conformally flat boundary metric, extending our earlier real Lorentzian construction. For admissible data with no spacelike Fourier support in a flat conformal frame, the physical response reduces to an integral over boundary light-cone cuts. Boundary improvements restore Fefferman--Graham (FG) gauge while preserving normalizability and the linearized Weyl tensor. We then reconstruct perturbations with general spacelike boundary momentum, including nonzero frequency and its zero-frequency limit, using explicit position-space generalized functions on real stress data. Boundary kernels are constructed for normalizable perturbations and sufficient conditions are derived for the reconstruction to converge. The results motivate controlled flat-space limits relevant to Bondi--Metzner--Sachs symmetries and celestial holography.

title: GRAVITY-RESOLVE: A comprehensive image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations with GRAVITY
comment: Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A) on October 24, 2026
summary: We aim to improve and extend the imaging capabilities of the GRAVITY beam combiner instrument of ESOs VLTI with respect to reconstruction software in the Galactic Center. We revise and develop the image reconstruction code GRAVITY-RESOLVE $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, which has been specifically developed to reconstruct stars in the Galactic Center with GRAVITY. The main objectives are to increase the limiting magnitude in GRAVITY images, reduce its computational runtime, and allow for a joint reconstruction of multiple, spatially separate datasets/pointings on sky. We apply $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ to recent GRAVITY data, featuring the implemented GRAVITY-faint mode as part of GRAVITY+, the upgrade of GRAVITY. We reconstruct visibility phases and amplitudes and present the first GRAVITY image reconstructed with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ from these quantities. We demonstrate NIR mosaicking with $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ by jointly reconstructing nine separately acquired datasets of 2025 into a single image on a scale of $\simeq 3390\ \text{AU}\times 3390\ \text{AU}$, corresponding to $409.6\ \text{mas}\times 409.6\ \text{mas}$. With dedicated injection tests of point sources into GRAVITY data, we estimate the limiting magnitude to be $m_{\text{K}}\ \simeq\ 20.0$ within a radius of $25\ \text{mas}$ around the field center when reconstructing from closure phases and visibility amplitudes. We report on the discovery of two new faint stars in the Galactic Center: S303 and S304. Finally, we find a decrease in computational runtime by a factor of at least $\sim10$. With $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$, we demonstrate GRAVITYs capabilities for NIR imaging. We show that $\text{G}^{\text{R}}$ is a fast, precise, and deep image reconstruction tool for Galactic Center observations, enabling the discovery of even more faint stars.

title: Linking a 152 GeV diphoton excess to dark matter and gravitational waves in the singlet-extended 2HDM
summary: We investigate the diphoton excesses near $152~\mathrm{GeV}$ accompanied by missing transverse momentum (MET) in the Type-I two-Higgs-doublet model extended by a complex scalar singlet, whose imaginary component serves as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone dark matter (DM) candidate $χ$. The signal arises from the cascade process $gg\to h_3\to h_2h_2\toγγχχ$, where $h_2$ is the scalar resonance near $152~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $h_3$ is a heavier CP-even scalar. After imposing the theoretical and experimental constraints, we identify parameter regions that accommodate at least one of the Low-MET and High-MET excesses within $1σ$ and simultaneously reproduce the observed DM relic density within an assumed $10\%$ theoretical uncertainty. A subset of these samples supports first-order electroweak phase transitions with substantial supercooling. For a three-year observation, selected samples yield gravitational-wave signals with signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) above $10$ at LISA, TianQin, DECIGO, and BBO. A representative benchmark that accommodates both excesses within their respective $1σ$ intervals and satisfies the relic-density requirement yields a three-year BBO SNR of approximately $173$.

title: Probing Scalar Polarization with Next-Generation Gravitational-Wave Detectors: The Roles of Detector Geometry and Source Inclination
summary: Gravitational-wave observations of compact binaries offer a direct way to test whether gravity admits polarizations beyond the two tensor modes of general relativity. We perform a forecast to assess how well future multi-messenger events will constrain the presence of scalar polarizations in gravitational waves. Performing binary neutron star injections, we forecast next-generation constraints on three modified gravity parameters in the PPE formalism: $α$ (tensor amplitude), $α_B$ (scalar amplitude) and $β$ (tensor and scalar phase). Cosmic Explorer (CE) and Einstein Telescope (ET) each tighten every parameter by 1--2 orders of magnitude over an O5 LIGO-Virgo network, with ET's triangular geometry giving a persistent $\approx2\times$ improvement over 2$\times$CE on the scalar-mode amplitude $α_B$ in both a GW170817-like and a second, representative BNS. We show that, if the sky position and luminosity distance are known from EM observations, adding an EM-based prior on the orbital inclination $ι$ narrows the $α_B$ constraint by $\approx56\times$ relative to an isotropic inclination prior, for a GW170817-like event. We also assess how EM inclination priors as well as assumptions on the neutron star equation of state may affect the inference on the scalar amplitude $α_B$. Overall, these results indicate that detector geometry and the availability of well-placed EM external information are both important levers --- alongside raw network sensitivity --- for next decade scalar-polarization tests.

title: At the EDGES of MADness: phenomenology of relic millicharged atomic dark matter
summary: Millicharged dark matter lives in a corner of parameter space that has been considerably shrinking over the past decades, due to constraints from cosmology, astrophysical systems, and ground-based experiments. A particularly interesting probe is the 21-cm absorption signal at Cosmic Dawn, which attracted interest in light of the EDGES claim: the reported excess absorption can be explained by millicharged dark matter with a fractional electric charge of~$10^{-6} \lesssim ε\lesssim 10^{-4}$, but it must be a subpercent of the total dark matter abundance to remain consistent with the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We show that very low fractions of millicharged dark matter naturally arise from atomic dark matter: a dark sector model that replicates the physics of standard atomic hydrogen. Dark ions undergo the process of dark recombination, leaving a relic ionized component that, in the presence of kinetic mixing, is naturally millicharged. We modify the cosmological Boltzmann solver CLASS to incorporate this scenario, and we investigate the parameter space of millicharged atomic dark matter (MAD) that is allowed by CMB, large-scale structure, and supernovae data. We find there are cosmologically viable regions of MAD parameter space that are consistent with laboratory and astrophysical bounds and also overlap with the EDGES-defined window. Although the EDGES result is likely not a Cosmic Dawn signal, MAD leaves distinctive cosmological signatures, accessible to upcoming 21-cm observations.

title: Probing Multi-formation Channels of Dark Matter-Deficient Galaxies in a Simulated Universe
comment: 28 pages, 21 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We investigate the formation and evolution of dark matter-deficient galaxies (DMDGs) using the IllustrisTNG100 cosmological hydrodynamical simulation. We define DMDGs as systems with a dark matter-to-stellar mass ratio below unity, and find two formation channels. In the first, galaxies that initially form within massive dark matter halos lose the majority of their dark matter and transition into DMDGs (acquired DMDGs). In the second, galaxies form with little or no dark matter from the beginning (inborn DMDGs). The two populations show distinct physical properties. Acquired DMDGs exhibit significant temporal variations in mass content, size, and kinematics, whereas inborn DMDGs show mild evolution. The former population tends to form closer to their nearest neighbor galaxies in large-scale overdense regions than the latter population does. We find that most stars in the inborn DMDGs form in situ. Their precursor gas is already metal-enriched and associated with other galaxies before formation. Tidal interactions and filamentary gas flows may contribute to the assembly of compact gas clumps, suggesting multiple formation pathways for inborn DMDGs. Our findings support the idea that there are at least two distinct channels to make galaxies dark matter deficient, which is important for understanding the formation mechanisms of these extreme systems.

title: Generalized Symmetries of QED$_4$ on Non-Spin Manifolds
summary: Generalized symmetries are sensitive to the tangential structure of spacetime. We study this interplay for massless QED on oriented non-spin four-manifolds, where the photon becomes a spin$^c$ connection and the path integral sums over spin$^c$ structures. The shifted flux quantization extends the magnetic 1-form symmetry into a $w_2$-twisted 1-form symmetry: its $2π$ rotation acts as a gravitational sign, fixed by the normal bundle of the surface the operator wraps. The obstruction to treating it as an ordinary magnetic 1-form symmetry is an order-two mixed magnetic-gravitational anomaly, which is classified by reduced oriented bordism and detected on the Wu manifold. In a fixed spin$^c$ sector, this anomaly is removable by a counterterm, so it is a property of the sum over spin$^c$ structures. We discuss its consequences for gapped, Coulomb, and Higgs phases. The chiral anomaly is governed by the index of the spin$^c$ Dirac operator, so rational chiral defects carry gravitational as well as electromagnetic responses. A spin$^c$ Hall topological field theory cancels the electromagnetic part but leaves a framing anomaly. At the level of anomaly inflow, this is canceled for every rational angle by stacking a neutral, generally noninvertible Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev layer. The same framing subtlety affects the chiral defects of QED on curved spin manifolds. The complex projective plane illustrates each of these features explicitly.

title: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background
summary: The stochastic gravitational-wave background from stellar-mass compact binaries is non-Gaussian since it is made up of a finite number of individual mergers. Over the years, several methods have been developed to search for this background beyond the standard cross-correlation statistic. We reformulate the data analysis problem for such astrophysical backgrounds in terms of the characteristic function of the data in multiple detectors, and show that the existing searches arise as different limiting cases. We also show that new searches can be constructed through different approximations of the characteristic function, which gives a concrete way to engineer suitable approximate sufficient statistics. To illustrate this framework in the context of a simple example, we use the formalism proposed here to analyze an exactly solvable toy model.

title: Proton GTMDs and Wigner Distributions in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model: Orbital Angular Momentum and Spin-Orbit Correlation with Sea Quarks
summary: We calculate the leading-twist vector and axial-vector quark generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) of the proton in the chiral quark soliton model, including both the discrete valence level and the regularized Dirac sea. We consider the isosinglet and isotriplet combinations of GTMDs at zero and nonzero skewness. At zero skewness, we construct Wigner distributions and resolve the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit correlation (SOC) densities in transverse position and momentum space, separately for quarks and antiquarks.
